sentences.zh: 解系

translations.literal: Xie Xi
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xi

sentences.zh: 解系，字少連，濟南著人也。

translations.literal: Xie Xi, courtesy name Shaolian, was a man of Zhu in Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xi, whose courtesy name was Shaolian, came from the district of Zhu in Jinan commandery.

sentences.zh: 父修，魏琅邪太守、梁州刺史，考績為天下第一。

translations.literal: His father Xiu, under Wei, was administrator of Langye and inspector of Liang province, and in merit evaluation was ranked first in the realm.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Xiu, had served Wei as administrator of Langye and as inspector of Liang province, earning the top merit rating in the empire.

sentences.zh: 武帝受禪，封梁鄒侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu received the abdication, [Xiu] was enfeoffed as marquis of Liangzou.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu accepted the Wei abdication, Xiu was invested as Marquis of Liangzou.

sentences.zh: 系及二弟結、育並清身潔己，甚得聲譽。

translations.literal: Xi together with his two younger brothers Jie and Yu all kept themselves and their persons clean, and enjoyed a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xi and his brothers Xie Jie and Xie Yu were alike in their spotless conduct and won wide esteem.

sentences.zh: 時荀勖門宗強盛，朝野畏憚之。

translations.literal: At that time Xun Xu’s clan was powerful and intimidating, and court and countryside feared them.
translations.idiomatic: In that era the house of Xun Xu was dominant enough that everyone at court and beyond walked in fear of it.

sentences.zh: 勖諸子謂系等曰：「我與卿為友，應向我公拜。

translations.literal: Xun’s sons said to Xi and the others, “We are friends with you; you ought to bow to my father.”
translations.idiomatic: The sons of Xun Xu told the Xie brothers, “We count you friends, so you ought to pay obeisance to our father.”

sentences.zh: 」勖又曰：「我與尊先使君親厚。

translations.literal: Xun also said, “I was on thick terms with your late worthy father.”
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu added, “I was on very close terms with your late father.”

sentences.zh: 」系曰：「不奉先君遺教。

translations.literal: Xi said, “I do not follow such alleged instruction from my late father.”
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xi replied, “Nothing my late father taught me obliges me to do that.”

sentences.zh: 公若與先君厚，往日哀頓，當垂書問。

translations.literal: “If you truly were close to my late father, in those days when our family was in mourning and distress, you should have sent letters asking after us.”
translations.idiomatic: “Had you really been intimate with him, you would have written with condolences when our house was in mourning and ruin.”

sentences.zh: 親厚之誨，非所敢承。

translations.literal: “As for your talk of close friendship, I dare not accept it.”
translations.idiomatic: “I cannot pretend that kind of friendship ever existed between our houses.”

sentences.zh: 」勖父子大慚，當世壯之。

translations.literal: Xun father and son were deeply ashamed, and people of the time thought him stalwart.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu and his sons were mortified, and contemporaries admired Xie Xi for his backbone.

sentences.zh: 後辟公府掾，歷中書黃門侍郎、散騎常侍、豫州刺史，遷尚書，出為雍州刺史、揚烈將軍、西戎校尉、假節。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned as a clerk to the excellencies’ offices; he passed through gentleman of the Yellow Gates in the secretariat and cavalier attendant in regular attendance, inspector of Yu province, was promoted to minister, then went out as inspector of Yong, general who raises might, colonel of the western tribes, with staff of authority.
translations.idiomatic: He later entered the central secretariat, rose to cavalier attendant in regular attendance and inspector of Yu province, then to secretary of the ministry of appointments before being posted as inspector of Yong, as General Who Spreads Might, as colonel of the Western Rong, and as bearer of the credential staff.

sentences.zh: 會氐羌叛，與征西將軍趙王倫討之。

translations.literal: When the Di and Qiang rebelled, he joined the western expedition general and King of Zhao, Sima Lun, to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Di and Qiang rose in rebellion, he campaigned alongside Sima Lun, the western expedition general and king of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 倫信用佞人孫秀，與系爭軍事，更相表奏。

translations.literal: Lun trusted the slanderous Sun Xiu; he and Xi quarreled over military affairs and each sent up memorials against the other.
translations.idiomatic: Lun favored the vicious favorite Sun Xiu; Sun and Xie wrangled over strategy and traded accusations at the throne.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知系守正不撓，而召倫還。

translations.literal: The court knew Xi held firm and did not bend, and summoned Lun back.
translations.idiomatic: The court knew Xie Xi had stood his ground without yielding and recalled Sima Lun to the capital.

sentences.zh: 系表殺秀以謝氐羌，不從。

translations.literal: Xi submitted a memorial calling for Xiu to be killed to appease the Di and Qiang; [the court] did not follow it.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Xi asked that Sun Xiu be executed as an offering to the Di and Qiang, but his plea was rejected.

sentences.zh: 倫、秀譖之，系坐免官，以白衣還第，闔門自守。

translations.literal: Lun and Xiu slandered him; Xi was therefore stripped of office, returned home in commoner’s garb, and shut his gate to keep to himself.
translations.idiomatic: Lun and Sun Xiu denounced him; Xie Xi lost his rank, went home in plain clothes, and locked his gates against the world.

sentences.zh: 及張華、裴頠之被誅也，倫、秀以宿憾收系兄弟。

translations.literal: When Zhang Hua and Pei Wei were executed, Lun and Xiu, harboring old resentment, seized Xi and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Hua and Pei Wei were put to death, Lun and Sun Xiu—still nursing old grudges—had the Xie brothers arrested.

sentences.zh: 梁王肜救系等，倫怒曰：「我于水中見蟹且惡之，況此人兄弟輕我邪！

translations.literal: King of Liang Sima Yong sought to save Xi and the others; Lun angrily said, “When I see a crab in the water I loathe it; how much more men whose brothers belittle me!
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liang Sima Yong intervened for the Xies, whereupon Lun growled, “I detest even a crab in a stream—let alone brothers who have slighted me!”

sentences.zh: 此而可忍，孰不可忍！

translations.literal: If this may be borne, what may not be borne!
translations.idiomatic: “If I tolerate this, there is nothing I cannot swallow!”

sentences.zh: 」肜苦爭之不得，遂害之，並戮其妻子。

translations.literal: ” Yong strove in vain to dissuade him; in the end they were put to death together with wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Yong argued until he had no leverage left; Lun had the Xies killed and wiped out their families.

sentences.zh: 後齊王冏起義時，以裴、解為冤首。

translations.literal: Later, when Prince of Qi Sima Jiong raised the righteous hosts, he named Pei and Xie as the first among the wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Sima Jiong of Qi rose in righteous rebellion, he listed Pei Wei and Xie Xi chief among the martyred worthies.

sentences.zh: 倫、秀既誅，冏乃奏曰：「臣聞興微繼絕，聖主之高政；

translations.literal: After Lun and Xiu were executed, Jiong memorialized, saying, “Your servant has heard that raising the fallen and continuing severed lines is the supreme governance of a sage ruler;
translations.idiomatic: Once Lun and Sun Xiu had been put to death, Jiong submitted a memorial: “I have heard that reviving ruined houses and restoring broken lines is the hallmark policy of a sage king;

sentences.zh: 貶惡嘉善，《春秋》之美談。

translations.literal: To degrade the wicked and praise the good is fine discourse in the Spring and Autumn.”
translations.idiomatic: while condemning villains and honoring goodness is what the Spring and Autumn Annals celebrate as true judgment.”

sentences.zh: 是以武王封比干之墓，表商容之閭，誠幽明之故有以相通也。

translations.literal: “Therefore King Wu of Zhou sealed Bi Gan’s tomb and marked Shang Rong’s lane, truly believing dark and bright have means by which they communicate.”
translations.idiomatic: King Wu of old rebuilt Bi Gan’s tomb and highlighted Shang Rong’s lane because justice must reach from this world into the next.”

sentences.zh: 孫秀逆亂，滅佐命之國，誅骨鯁之臣，以斫喪王室，肆其虐戾，功臣之後，多見泯滅。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu rebelled and brought chaos, extinguishing states that had aided the founding mandate, executing ministers of unbending bone who had propped up the royal house, thereby hacking at the dynasty and indulging cruelty and violence; many descendants of meritorious servants perished.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu’s coup gutted the families that had sealed the Jin mandate, slaughtered ministers bold enough to speak truth, and ravaged the house of Jin; lineages of old heroes were mutilated wholesale.”

sentences.zh: 至如張華、裴頠，各以見憚取誅于時，系、結同以羔羊被害，歐陽建等無罪而死，百姓憐之。

translations.literal: As for Zhang Hua and Pei Wei, each through being feared was executed in that time; Xi and Jie alike fell victim like sacrificial lambs; Ouyang Jian and others died without guilt; the common people pitied them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua and Pei Wei were killed simply because others feared them; Xie Xi and Xie Jie died like lambs led to slaughter; Ouyang Jian and the rest were innocent—ordinary folk still weep for them.”

sentences.zh: 陛下更日月之光照，布惟新之明命，然此等未蒙恩理。

translations.literal: Your Majesty by the shining of sun and moon has spread a renewing mandate of illumination, yet these persons have not yet received grace and reasoned disposition.”
translations.idiomatic: “Under Your Majesty’s luminous rule such men deserve redress, yet they still await recognition.”

sentences.zh: 昔欒郤降在皁隸，而《春秋》傳其人；

translations.literal: “Formerly Luan and Xi fell to the status of grooms, yet the Zuo Commentary transmitted them;
translations.idiomatic: “The Zuo Tradition still commemorated Luan and Xi after they sank to stable-hands—because merit must outlive misfortune.”

sentences.zh: 幽王絕功臣之後，棄賢者子孫，而詩人以為刺。

translations.literal: King You of Zhou cut off the posterity of merit ministers and cast away worthies’ descendants, and the poets took this as satire.”
translations.idiomatic: King You, by abandoning the heirs of loyal ministers, earned the Classic of Poetry’s bitter satire—may we never repeat it.”

sentences.zh: 臣備忝右職，思竭股肱，獻納愚誠。

translations.literal: Your servant occupies the right column unworthily and wishes to exhaust arms and legs, offering foolish sincerity.”
translations.idiomatic: “Though unworthy to stand at Your right, I beg to exhaust my strength in blunt counsel.”

sentences.zh: 若合聖意，可群官通議。

translations.literal: If it accords with sage intent, all officials may deliberate jointly.”
translations.idiomatic: “If any of this reflects sage intent, let the full bureaucracy debate it together.”

sentences.zh: 」八坐議以「系等清公正直，為奸邪所疾，無罪橫戮，冤痛已甚。

translations.literal: ” The Eight Seats deliberated, saying, “Xi and the others were pure, fair, and upright; by wicked and crooked men they were resented; without crime they were violently executed; wrong and pain are already extreme.
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Senior Ministers replied: “Xie Xi and his brothers were upright officials destroyed by villains; they were slaughtered without crime, and their grievance cries to Heaven.”

sentences.zh: 如大司馬所啟，彰明枉直，顯宣當否，使冤魂無愧無恨，為恩大矣。

translations.literal: As the grand marshal reported, to make clear the bent and straight, to show plainly what is fitting or not, so that wronged souls have neither shame nor resentment, is great kindness.
translations.idiomatic: “Grant the grand marshal’s request: set the record straight so their shades may rest—that would be the ultimate grace.”

sentences.zh: 」，追贈光祿大夫，改葬，加弔祭焉。

translations.literal: ”, posthumously he was awarded grand master of the palace, reburied, and condolence sacrifices were added.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously named Xie Xi grand master of the palace and, with full rites, had him reinterred and honored with mourning sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 結字叔連，少與系齊名。

translations.literal: Jie, courtesy name Shulian, in youth shared fame with Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Jie, courtesy Shulian, was already renowned alongside his elder brother while still young.

sentences.zh: 辟公府掾，累遷黃門侍郎，歷散騎常恃、豫州刺史、魏郡太守、御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was summoned clerk to the excellencies’ offices; he ascended to gentleman of the Yellow Gates, passed through cavalier attendant in regular attendance, inspector of Yu province, prefect of Wei, and palace secretary in charge of law.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as a clerk in the Three Excellencies’ offices, he rose to gentleman of the Yellow Gate, then cavalier attendant in regular attendance, inspector of Yu, prefect of Wei commandery, and imperial secretary.

sentences.zh: 時孫秀亂關中，結在都，坐議秀罪應誅，秀由是致憾。

translations.literal: At that time Sun Xiu brought chaos to Guanzhong; Jie was in the capital; sitting in deliberation he maintained Xiu’s crime deserved execution; Xiu therefore nursed a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Xiu ravaged the Guanzhong region, Xie Jie—still at court—argued that Sun deserved death; from that day Sun never forgave him.

sentences.zh: 及系被害，結亦同戮。

translations.literal: When Xi was murdered, Jie was likewise executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Xi was killed, Xie Jie died with him.

sentences.zh: 女適裴氏，明日當嫁，而禍起，裴氏欲認活之，女曰：「家既若此，我何活為！

translations.literal: His daughter was betrothed to the Pei family; the next day she was to be married, but disaster arose; the Pei wanted to claim her alive; the girl said, “The family being thus, what am I to live for!
translations.idiomatic: His daughter was pledged to the Pei clan; her wedding was due the next morning when catastrophe struck. The Peis tried to swear she had never been a Xie. The girl said, “If my family is destroyed, why should I live?”

sentences.zh: 」亦坐死。

translations.literal: ” She too sat [among the condemned] and died.
translations.idiomatic: She accepted condemnation with her kin and walked to execution.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遂議革舊制，女不從坐，由結女始也。

translations.literal: The court then deliberated to change the old statute: daughters should not sit joint guilt; it began from Jie’s daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Her case forced the court to abolish collective guilt for daughters—that reform began with Xie Jie’s child.

sentences.zh: 後贈結光祿大夫，改葬，加弔祭。

translations.literal: Later Jie was posthumously awarded grand master of the palace, reburied, with added condolence sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Later the throne posthumously appointed Xie Jie grand master of the palace, reburied him, and added state sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 結弟育，字稚連，名亞二兄。

translations.literal: Jie’s younger brother Yu, courtesy name Zhilian, ranked below the two elder brothers in name.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xie Yu, courtesy Zhilian, stood a notch below his famous brothers in reputation.

sentences.zh: 歷公府掾、太子洗馬、尚書郎、衛軍長史、弘農太守，與二兄俱被害，妻子徙邊。

translations.literal: He passed through clerks of the excellencies, attendant of the heir-apparent’s palace, gentleman of the ministry of appointments, staff director for the guard army, prefect of Hongnong; together with the two elder brothers he suffered execution; wives and children were exiled to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He held successive posts—clerk in the central offices, crown prince’s groom, ministry gentleman, chief clerk to the guards army, and governor of Hongnong—before being executed with his brothers; their wives and children were banished beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 孫旂

translations.literal: Sun Qi
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qi

sentences.zh: 孫旂，字伯旗，樂安人也。

translations.literal: Sun Qi, courtesy name Boqi, was a man of Le’an.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qi, courtesy Boqi, hailed from Le’an commandery.

sentences.zh: 父曆，魏晉際為幽州刺史、右將軍。

translations.literal: His father Li, at the Wei–Jin transition, was inspector of You province and general of the right.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sun Li, during the handover from Wei to Jin, had served as inspector of You and general of the right.

sentences.zh: 旂潔靜，少自修立。

translations.literal: Qi was pure and quiet, and from youth cultivated himself.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qi was reserved and meticulous, polishing his conduct from an early age.

sentences.zh: 察孝廉，累遷黃門侍郎，出為荊州刺史，名位與二解相亞。

translations.literal: Recommended filial and incorrupt, he ascended to gentleman of the Yellow Gates, went out as inspector of Jing province, and his name and rank were next after the two Xies.
translations.idiomatic: Raised on the filial-and-incorrupt recommendation, he advanced to gentleman of the Yellow Gate and then inspector of Jing, ranking just below the Xie brothers in prestige.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，徵拜太子詹事，轉衛尉，坐武庫火，免官。

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era he was summoned grand mentor to the heir apparent, transferred to commandant of the guard, and for an arsenal fire was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongxi he was recalled as mentor to the crown prince, rotated into commandant of the guards, then dismissed after the imperial armory caught fire.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，出為兗州刺史，遷平南將軍、假節。

translations.literal: After more than a year he went out as inspector of Yanzhou, promoted general who pacifies the south, with staff of authority.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he returned to provincial duty as inspector of Yanzhou and general who pacifies the south, bearing the credential staff.

sentences.zh: 旂子弼及弟子髦、輔、琰四人，並有吏材，稱於當世，遂與孫秀合族。

translations.literal: Qi’s son Bi and his nephews Mao, Fu, and Yan—four men—all had official talent, famed in their generation, and therefore combined clanship with Sun Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sun Bi and nephews Sun Mao, Sun Fu, and Sun Yan—all four gifted administrators—won contemporary fame and merged their lineage with Sun Xiu’s branch.

sentences.zh: 及趙王倫起事，夜從秀開神武門下觀閱器械。

translations.literal: When King of Zhao Sima Lun raised the coup, at night they followed Xiu to open Shenwu Gate below and review arms and equipment.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Lun mobilized his coup, they slipped out at night with Sun Xiu to unbar Shenwu Gate and inspect weapons.

sentences.zh: 兄弟旬月相次為公府掾、尚書郎。

translations.literal: Within a month in succession they became clerks of the excellencies and gentlemen of the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Inside a single month each rose to secretariat posts—clerks in the excellencies and gentlemen of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 弼又為中堅將軍，領尚書左丞，轉為上將軍，領射聲校尉。

translations.literal: Bi also became sturdy-core general, concurrent supervisor of the left in the ministry, transferred to senior general, concurrent colonel of the whistling-arrows corps.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Bi advanced to stalwart-core general while leading the left section of the Secretariat, then to supreme general overseeing the whistling-arrows garrison.

sentences.zh: 髦為武衛將軍，領太子詹事。

translations.literal: Mao became guard general of the martial guard, concurrently grand mentor to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Mao became martial guard general while doubling as mentor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 琰為武威將軍，領太子左率。

translations.literal: Yan became mighty-invasion general, concurrently colonel commanding the heir’s left guard.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yan became general of awe-inspiring might while commanding the crown prince’s left escort.

sentences.zh: 皆賜爵開國郡侯。

translations.literal: All were enfeoffed county marquises with founding lineages.
translations.idiomatic: Each received a frontier-establishing marquisate at commandery rank.

sentences.zh: 推崇旂為車騎將軍、開府。

translations.literal: They promoted Qi to chariot-and-cavalry general with independent administration.
translations.idiomatic: On their recommendation Sun Qi was raised to chariot-and-cavalry general with independent staff.

sentences.zh: 初，旂以弼等受署偽朝，遣小息回責讓弼等，以過差之事，必為家禍。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Bi and the others had accepted posts in the usurping court, Qi sent his younger son Hui back to rebuke Bi and the others that matters of excessive fault would surely bring family calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Sun Qi, horrified that his son and nephews had taken office under the usurper, dispatched his youngest son Sun Hui home to berate them—warning that overreaching ambition would consume the clan.

sentences.zh: 弼等終不從，旂制之不可，但慟哭而已。

translations.literal: Bi and the others in the end did not obey; Qi could not restrain them and could only wail in tears.
translations.idiomatic: They refused to listen; Sun Qi could not control them and could only weep in despair.

sentences.zh: 及齊王冏起義，四子皆伏誅。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qi Sima Jiong raised the righteous hosts, the four sons were all executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Jiong rose in righteous rebellion, all four youths were arrested and executed.

sentences.zh: 襄陽太守宗岱承冏檄斬旂，夷三族。

translations.literal: Prefect of Xiangyang Zong Dai, acting on Jiong’s summons, beheaded Qi and extirpated three clans.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Dai, governor of Xiangyang, answering Jiong’s warrant, executed Sun Qi and extirpated three generations of kin.

sentences.zh: 弟尹，字文旗，歷陳留、陽平太守，早卒。

translations.literal: Younger brother Yin, courtesy Wenqi, served as prefect of Chenliu and Yangping, and died early.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qi’s younger brother Sun Yin, courtesy Wenqi, governed Chenliu and Yangping before dying young.

sentences.zh: 孟觀

translations.literal: Meng Guan
translations.idiomatic: Meng Guan

sentences.zh: 孟觀，字叔時，渤海東光人也。

translations.literal: Meng Guan, courtesy name Shushi, was a man of Dongguang in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Guan, courtesy Shushi, came from Dongguang county in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 少好讀書，解天文。

translations.literal: In youth he loved reading and understood astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he loved books and mastered astronomy.

sentences.zh: 惠帝即位，稍遷殿中中郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui ascended, he gradually rose to palace court gentleman of the center.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Hui took the throne he rose slowly to middle gentleman of the palace bureau.

sentences.zh: 賈后悖婦姑之禮，陰欲誅楊駿而廢太后，因駿專權，數言之於帝，又使人諷觀。

translations.literal: Empress Jia violated the rites between wife and mother-in-law; secretly wishing to execute Yang Jun and depose the empress dowager, because Jun monopolized power, she repeatedly spoke of this to the emperor and also sent persons to hint to Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia despised the rites owed to a mother-in-law; plotting to kill Yang Jun and depose the empress dowager, she harped on Yang’s monopoly of power before the emperor and nudged Meng Guan to back her.

sentences.zh: 會楚王瑋將討駿，觀受賈后旨宣詔，頗加誣其事。

translations.literal: When King of Chu Sima Wei was about to punish Jun, Guan received Empress Jia’s secret edict to proclaim the edict, somewhat fabricating the affair.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Wei of Chu marched against Yang Jun, Meng Guan relayed the empress’s secret instructions, embellishing the charges as he proclaimed the decree.

sentences.zh: 及駿誅，以觀為黃門侍郎，特給親信四十人。

translations.literal: When Jun was executed, Guan was made gentleman of the Yellow Gates, especially given forty confidential attendants.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang’s fall he was promoted to gentleman of the Yellow Gate with forty handpicked attendants.

sentences.zh: 遷積弩將軍，封上穀郡公。

translations.literal: He was transferred to rapid-crossbow general and enfeoffed duke of Shanggu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to rapid-crossbow general and was enfeoffed duke of Shanggu commandery.

sentences.zh: 氐帥齊萬年反於關中，眾數十萬，諸將覆敗相繼。

translations.literal: Di chieftain Qi Wannian rebelled in Guanzhong; the hosts numbered several hundred thousand; generals in succession were crushed and defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The Di leader Qi Wannian rebelled in Guanzhong at the head of hundreds of thousands; imperial generals fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 中書令陳准、監張華，以趙、梁諸王在關中，雍容貴戚，進不貪功，退不懼罪，士卒雖眾，不為之用，周處喪敗，職此之由，上下離心，難以勝敵。

translations.literal: Palace Secretariat Director Chen Zhun and Supervisor Zhang Hua held that the kings of Zhao and Liang in Guanzhong, being relaxed nobles of the imperial kindred, advanced without coveting merit and retreated without fearing punishment; though soldiers were numerous, they would not work for them; Zhou Chu’s rout for this reason came about; high and low were sundered in heart and hard to use against the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat director Chen Zhun and overseer Zhang Hua argued that the Wei princes in Guanzhong—pampered imperial in-laws—neither pressed for glory nor feared disgrace, so their hosts would not fight; Zhou Chu’s disaster stemmed from that fatal split between commanders and men.

sentences.zh: 以觀沈毅，有文武材用，乃啟觀討之。

translations.literal: Because Guan was deep and resolute and had civil and military talent and use, they therefore opened [a mission for] Guan to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore proposed Meng Guan—tough, steady, and skilled in arms and letters—to take the field.

sentences.zh: 觀所領宿衛兵，皆趫捷勇悍，並統關中士卒，身當矢石，大戰十數，皆破之，生擒萬年，威懾氐羌。

translations.literal: The palace guard troops Guan led were all nimble, brave, and fierce; he also commanded Guanzhong soldiers, himself stood before arrows and stones, fought great battles over ten rounds, all defeated them, captured Wannian alive, and awe overawed the Di and Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: The palace guards he led were picked for speed and ferocity; blending them with Guanzhong levies, he met flights of arrows and stones himself, shattered Qi Wannian’s army in more than a dozen major clashes, took Wannian alive, and cowed every Di and Qiang band.

sentences.zh: 轉東羌校尉，徵拜右將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred colonel of the eastern Qiang, summoned as general of the right.
translations.idiomatic: He rotated to colonel of the eastern Qiang and was recalled as general of the right.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫篡位，以觀所在著績，署為安南將軍、監河北諸軍事、假節，屯宛。

translations.literal: When King of Zhao Sima Lun usurped, because of Guan’s distinctions wherever posted, he appointed him general who pacifies the south, overseer of all Hebei military affairs, with staff of authority, stationed at Wan.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Lun seized the throne, he prized Meng Guan’s battle record and named him general who pacifies the south, overseer of military affairs north of the Yellow River, with credential staff, stationed at Wan.

sentences.zh: 觀子平為淮南王允前鋒將軍，討倫，戰死。

translations.literal: Guan’s son Ping was vanguard general to Prince Huainan Sima Yun in the campaign against Lun and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His son Meng Ping served Prince Huainan Sima Yun as vanguard general against Lun and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 孫秀以觀杖兵在外，假言平為允兵所害，贈積弩將軍以安觀。

translations.literal: Sun Xiu, because Guan held troops abroad, falsely claimed Ping had been killed by Yun’s troops, posthumously awarding rapid-crossbow general to pacify Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu, wary that Meng Guan still camped beyond Luoyang with an army, spread word that Meng Ping had been murdered by Yun’s soldiers and soothed the father with a posthumous rapid-crossbow generalship.

sentences.zh: 義軍既起，多勸觀應齊王冏，觀以紫宮帝坐無他變，謂倫應之，遂不從眾議而為倫守。

translations.literal: Once the righteous armies rose, many urged Guan to respond to Prince of Qi Sima Jiong; Guan held that in the Purple Palace the imperial seat showed no other change, deeming Lun matched it, and therefore did not follow the multitude’s counsel but defended for Lun.
translations.idiomatic: When the loyalist hosts mobilized, counsellors begged Meng Guan to declare for Sima Jiong; he gazed at the imperial seat asterism, detected no celestial warning, decided Lun matched Heaven’s will, and chose to ignore the clamor—remaining Lun’s partisan.

sentences.zh: 及帝反正，永饒冶令空桐機斬觀首，傳於洛陽，遂夷三族。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned to normality, Kongtong Ji, magistrate of Yongrao foundry, cut off Guan’s head and sent it to Luoyang; then three clans were extirpated.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor was restored, Kongtong Ji, magistrate of the Yongrao foundry office, struck off Meng Guan’s head and forwarded it to Luoyang before annihilating three generations of his kin.

sentences.zh: 牽秀

translations.literal: Qian Xiu
translations.idiomatic: Qian Xiu

sentences.zh: 牽秀，字成叔，武邑觀津人也。

translations.literal: Qian Xiu, courtesy name Chengshu, was a man of Guanjin in Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Xiu, courtesy Chengshu, came from Guanjin in Wuyi commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖招，魏雁門太守。

translations.literal: Grandfather Zhao was administrator of Wild Goose Gate under Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qian Zhao had served Wei as administrator of Yanmen commandery.

sentences.zh: 秀博辯有文才，性豪俠，弱冠得美名，為太保衛瓘、尚書崔洪所知。

translations.literal: Xiu was broadly disputatious and had literary talent; his nature was heroic and chivalrous; at weak-crown he obtained a fine reputation, known to grand protector Wei Guan and minister Cui Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Xiu was eloquent and literary, swaggering and generous; before he turned twenty he was already famed, noticed by grand tutor Wei Guan and minister Cui Hong.

sentences.zh: 太康中，調補新安令，累遷司空從事中郎。

translations.literal: In Taikang he was transferred and supplemented as magistrate of Xin’an, ascending to aide in the ministry of works.
translations.idiomatic: During Taikang he was reassigned magistrate of Xin’an, then rose to senior clerk in the ministry of works.

sentences.zh: 與帝舅王愷素相輕侮，愷諷司隸荀愷奏秀夜在道中載高平國守士田興妻。

translations.literal: With the emperor’s uncle Wang Kai he had long mutually disparaged each other; Kai had metropolitan commandant Xun Kai memorialize that Xiu by night on the road carried off the wife of field officer Tian Xing of the Gaoping princedom.
translations.idiomatic: He despised the emperor’s uncle Wang Kai; Wang Kai persuaded metropolitan commandant Xun Kai to impeach Qian Xiu for abducting Tian Xing’s wife on the highway at night.

sentences.zh: 秀即表訴被誣，論愷穢行，文辭亢厲，以譏抵外戚。

translations.literal: Xiu immediately submitted a memorial stating he had been slandered, discussing Kai’s filthy conduct, the phrasing forceful and harsh, thereby satirizing the outer kin.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Xiu fired back a shrill memorial proclaiming his innocence and airing Wang Kai’s debauchery, mocking the consort clan in blistering prose.

sentences.zh: 于時朝臣雖多證明其行，而秀盛名美譽由是而損，遂坐免官。

translations.literal: At that time though many court ministers bore witness to clear his conduct, Xiu’s great name and fine reputation thereby suffered loss, and he therefore sat stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Even though colleagues vouched for him, his luster never recovered and he was cashiered.

sentences.zh: 後司空張華請為長史。

translations.literal: Later minister of works Zhang Hua requested him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhang Hua, minister of works, recruited him as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 秀任氣，好為將帥。

translations.literal: Xiu indulged temperament and liked to be generals and commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Xiu answered to no one and longed for field command.

sentences.zh: 張昌作亂，長沙王乂遣秀討昌，秀出關，因奔成都王穎。

translations.literal: When Zhang Chang rebelled, Prince Changsha Sima Yi sent Xiu to punish Chang; Xiu went out of the pass and thereupon fled to Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Chang revolted, Prince Changsha Sima Yi dispatched Qian Xiu to suppress him; Qian marched through the passes and bolted straight to Sima Ying’s camp in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 穎伐乂，以秀為冠軍將軍，與陸機、王粹等共為河橋之役。

translations.literal: Ying campaigned against Yi, appointing Xiu champion general, together with Lu Ji, Wang Cui and others in the battle at the He Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying, marching against his brother, named Qian Xiu champion general alongside Lu Ji and Wang Cui for the Heqiao campaign.

sentences.zh: 機戰敗，秀證成其罪，又諂事黃門孟玖，故見親於穎。

translations.literal: When Ji was defeated in battle, Xiu testified to establish his guilt, and also flattered the Yellow Gate Meng Jiu, therefore being held dear by Ying.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu Ji collapsed at Heqiao, Qian Xiu twisted testimony to damn him and curried favor with eunuch Meng Jiu, which won Sima Ying’s trust.

sentences.zh: 惠帝西幸長安，以秀為尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui went west to fortunate Chang’an, Xiu was made minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hui was driven west to Chang’an, Qian Xiu was appointed minister of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 秀少在京輦，見司隸劉毅奏事而扼腕慷慨，自謂居司直之任，當能激濁揚清；

translations.literal: Xiu in youth was in the capital precincts; seeing Metropolitan Commandant Liu Yi submit business and wring wrist in fervent indignation, he himself thought that occupying the straight-office duty he would be able to whip the turbid and lift the clear;
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Qian Xiu watched metropolitan commandant Liu Yi present memorials with clenched-fist passion and imagined that, once he held the censor’s mace himself, he would scour corruption and trumpet integrity;

sentences.zh: 處鼓鞞之間，必建將帥之勳。

translations.literal: placed among drums and leather, he would surely establish the merit of generals and commanders.
translations.idiomatic: and that amid the thunder of war drums he would win the laurels of a field commander.

sentences.zh: 及在常伯納言，亦未曾有規獻弼違之奇也。

translations.literal: When he was among the regular attendants and remonstrance speakers, he also never had the exceptional merit of remonstrating, offering counsel, aiding the ruler, or correcting errors.
translations.idiomatic: Even after he rose to palace spokesman and chief remonstrant, he never mustered the kind of blunt counsel that steadies a throne.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒甚親任之。

translations.literal: Prince of Hejian Sima Yong was very intimate with him and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yong, prince of Hejian, kept him close and relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 關東諸軍奉迎大駕，以秀為平北將軍，鎮馮翊。

translations.literal: The armies east of the pass escorted the imperial carriage; they appointed Xiu general who pacifies the north and stationed him at Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern coalition, intent on restoring the emperor, named Qian Xiu general who pacifies the north and posted him to Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 秀與顒將馬瞻等將輔顒以守關中，顒密遣使就東海王越求迎，越遣將麋晃等迎顒。

translations.literal: Xiu with Yong’s generals Ma Zhan and others were to assist Yong in defending Guanzhong; Yong secretly sent an envoy to Prince of Donghai Sima Yue seeking a welcome; Yue dispatched generals Mi Huang and others to escort Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Xiu camped with Yong’s generals such as Ma Zhan to hold the Guanzhong line, while Yong secretly begged Sima Yue for rescue; Yue answered by sending Mi Huang and other officers to fetch him.

sentences.zh: 時秀擁眾在馮翊，晃不敢進。

translations.literal: At that time Xiu held a host at Fengyi; Huang did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Xiu still commanded a large force at Fengyi, so Mi Huang dared not push forward.

sentences.zh: 顒長史楊騰前不應越軍，懼越討之，欲取秀以自效，與馮翊大姓諸嚴詐稱顒命，使秀罷兵，秀信之，騰遂殺秀於萬年。

translations.literal: Yong’s chief clerk Yang Teng had earlier refused to cooperate with Yue’s army; fearing Yue would punish him, he wished to seize Xiu to prove his loyalty; with powerful Fengyi families surnamed Yan he forged Yong’s order telling Xiu to disband his troops; Xiu believed it, and Teng then killed Xiu at Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Teng, Yong’s chief clerk, had defied Yue’s troops and now hoped to buy pardon by murdering Qian Xiu; he and the Yan magnates of Fengyi forged an order to disarm him, lured him out, and cut him down at Wannian.

sentences.zh: 繆播

translations.literal: Miao Bo
translations.idiomatic: Miao Bo

sentences.zh: 繆播，字宣則，蘭陵人也。

translations.literal: Miao Bo, courtesy name Xuancao, was a man of Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Bo, courtesy Xuancao, came from Lanling.

sentences.zh: 父悅，光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His father Yue was grand master of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: His father Miao Yue had held the post of grand master of the palace.

sentences.zh: 播才思清辯，有意義。

translations.literal: Bo’s talent and thoughts were clear and disputatious; he had meaningful purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Bo combined a lucid intellect with eloquence and a strong sense of public duty.

sentences.zh: 高密王泰為司空，以播為祭酒，累遷太弟中庶子。

translations.literal: Prince of Gaomi Sima Tai was minister of works; he made Bo libationer; [Bo] ascended to junior mentor in the senior heir’s household.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Tai of Gaomi served as minister of works, he took Miao Bo as libationer; Bo later rose to junior mentor in the heir apparent’s household.

sentences.zh: 惠帝幸長安，河間王顒欲挾天子令諸侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui went to Chang’an, Prince of Hejian Sima Yong wished to seize the Son of Heaven to command the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Hui was driven to Chang’an, Sima Yong of Hejian meant to hold the emperor hostage and dictate to the regional lords.

sentences.zh: 東海王越將起兵奉迎天子，以播父時故吏，委以心膂。

translations.literal: Prince of Donghai Sima Yue would raise troops to escort the sovereign; because Bo’s father had been Yue’s former subordinate, [Yue] entrusted him as backbone and heart.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue of Donghai prepared a loyal rising to bring the ruler home; because Miao Bo’s father had once served under him, Yue treated Bo as a confidant.

sentences.zh: 播從弟右衛率胤，顒前妃之弟也。

translations.literal: Bo’s cousin, captain of the right guard Yin, was the younger brother of Yong’s former consort.
translations.idiomatic: Bo’s kinsman Miao Yin, captain of the right guard, was the brother of Yong’s divorced consort.

sentences.zh: 越遣播、胤詣長安說顒，令奉帝還洛，約與顒分陝為伯。

translations.literal: Yue dispatched Bo and Yin to Chang’an to persuade Yong, ordering him to return the emperor to Luoyang, agreeing to divide the realm at Shan and each be a lord.
translations.idiomatic: Yue sent Bo and Yin west to talk Yong into releasing the court to Luoyang, offering to split authority at the Shan pass like the ancient dukes of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 播、胤素為顒所敬信，既相見，虛懷從之。

translations.literal: Bo and Yin had long been respected and trusted by Yong; once they met, [Yong] with open mind followed them.
translations.idiomatic: Yong had always respected the two men; when they arrived he listened with unusual candor.

sentences.zh: 顒將張方自以罪重，懼為誅首，謂顒曰：「今據形勝之地，國富兵強，奉天子以號令，誰敢不服！

translations.literal: Yong’s general Zhang Fang, thinking himself deeply guilty, feared being the first executed, and said to Yong, “Now we hold commanding terrain, the state is rich and the army strong; upholding the Son of Heaven to issue commands—who will dare not submit!
translations.idiomatic: General Zhang Fang, terrified that he would be singled out for execution, urged Yong: “We occupy the strategic west, our treasury is full, and our spears are many; with the emperor in hand we can issue orders that no one dares refuse!”

sentences.zh: 」顒惑方所謀，猶豫不決。

translations.literal: ” Yong was misled by Fang’s plan and hesitated undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Yong let Zhang Fang’s argument confuse him and stalled.

sentences.zh: 方惡播、胤為越遊說，陰欲殺之。

translations.literal: Fang hated Bo and Yin for lobbying for Yue and secretly wished to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fang despised Bo and Yin as Yue’s mouthpieces and plotted their murder.

sentences.zh: 播等亦慮方為難，不敢復言。

translations.literal: Bo and others also feared Fang would make trouble and dared not speak again.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys, fearing Zhang Fang’s temper, fell silent.

sentences.zh: 時越兵鋒甚盛，顒深憂之，播、胤乃復說顒，急斬方以謝，可不勞而安。

translations.literal: At that time Yue’s military edge was very keen; Yong was deeply worried; Bo and Yin then again persuaded Yong, urgently to execute Fang to apologize, and without labor there would be peace.
translations.idiomatic: As Yue’s armies tightened the noose, Bo and Yin renewed their plea: behead Zhang Fang, offer his head as apology, and the east would stand down without another battle.

sentences.zh: 顒從之，於是斬方以謝山東諸侯。

translations.literal: Yong followed it; thereupon he executed Fang to apologize to the lords east of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Yong yielded and executed Zhang Fang, sending his head to placate the eastern alliance.

sentences.zh: 顒後悔之，又以兵距越，屢為越所敗。

translations.literal: Yong afterward regretted it and again used troops to resist Yue, repeatedly being defeated by Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He soon regretted the concession, reopened hostilities against Yue, and lost every clash.

sentences.zh: 帝反舊都，播亦從太弟還洛，契闊艱難，深相親狎。

translations.literal: The emperor returned to the old capital; Bo also followed the senior heir back to Luoyang; they had gone through hardship together and were deeply intimate.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to Luoyang, Bo accompanied the heir apparent through every danger, and the two men grew inseparable.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，太弟即帝位，是為懷帝，以播為給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, the senior heir succeeded—this is Emperor Huai—and appointed Bo gentleman at the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: After Hui’s death that heir became Emperor Huai and named Bo gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 俄轉侍中，徙中書令，任遇日隆，專管詔命。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred to palace attendant, moved to palace secretariat director; favor daily grew; he solely managed edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Within months Bo rose to palace attendant, then director of the secretariat, monopolizing the drafting of imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 時越威權自己，帝力不能討，心甚惡之。

translations.literal: At that time Yue’s authority was his own; the emperor’s strength could not punish him, and in his heart he greatly hated it.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue answered to no one; the emperor lacked the power to curb him and nursed a bitter grudge.

sentences.zh: 以播、胤等有公輔之量，又盡忠于國，故委以心膂。

translations.literal: Because Bo and Yin and others had the capacity of assistant ministers of state, and also were utterly loyal to the state, therefore [the emperor] entrusted them as backbone and heart.
translations.idiomatic: Huai trusted Bo, Yin, and their circle as men of ministerial stature who would serve the throne, not Yue’s faction.

sentences.zh: 越懼為己害，因入朝，以兵入宮，執播等於帝側。

translations.literal: Yue feared they would become a harm to himself; therefore entering court, he led troops into the palace and seized Bo and others beside the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yue struck first: he marched into the palace with soldiers and dragged Bo and his allies from the emperor’s side.

sentences.zh: 帝歎曰：「奸臣賊子無世無之，不自我先，不自我後，哀哉！

translations.literal: The emperor sighed, saying, “Wicked ministers and rebel sons exist in no age without them; not before myself, not after myself—alas!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor groaned, “Treachery dogs every age—yet why must it fall on my reign?”

sentences.zh: 」起執播等手，涕泗歔欷，不能自禁。

translations.literal: ” He rose and grasped Bo and others’ hands, weeping and sobbing, unable to restrain himself.
translations.idiomatic: He stood, clasped their hands, and wept until he could not speak.

sentences.zh: 越遂害之。

translations.literal: Yue then killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Yue had them executed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 朝野憤惋，咸曰：「善人，國之紀也，而加虐焉，其能終乎！

translations.literal: Court and countryside resented in sorrow, all saying, “Good men are the cords of the state, yet violence was added to them—can it end well!
translations.idiomatic: Across the capital voices cried, “The good are the backbone of the realm—yet you slaughter them; can the dynasty endure?”

sentences.zh: 」及越薨，帝贈播衛尉，祠以少牢。

translations.literal: ” When Yue died, the emperor posthumously awarded Bo commandant of the guard and sacrificed to him with the minor victim.
translations.idiomatic: After Yue’s death Huai posthumously named Bo commandant of the guard and offered him the lesser victim at the state altar.

sentences.zh: 胤字休祖，安平獻王外孫也，與播名譽略齊。

translations.literal: Yin, courtesy name Xiuzu, was the maternal grandson of Prince Xian of Anping, and with Bo his reputation was roughly equal.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Yin, courtesy Xiuzu, was a grandson on the distaff side of Prince Xian of Anping and matched Bo in reputation.

sentences.zh: 初為尚書郎，後遷太弟左衛率，轉魏郡太守。

translations.literal: First he was gentleman of the ministries, later promoted left captain of the guard for the senior heir, transferred prefect of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a ministry gentleman, became left captain of the heir’s guard, and then prefect of Wei commandery.

sentences.zh: 及王浚軍逼鄴，石超等大敗，胤奔東海王越於徐州，越使胤與播俱入關，而所說得行，大駕東還。

translations.literal: When Wang Jun’s army pressed Ye, Shi Chao and others were greatly defeated; Yin fled to Prince of Donghai Yue at Xu province; Yue sent Yin together with Bo both to enter the pass, and the persuasion succeeded, the great chariot returned east.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jun threatened Ye and Shi Chao’s host collapsed, Yin fled to Sima Yue in Xu; Yue sent him with Bo into the pass, their diplomacy secured the emperor’s return east.

sentences.zh: 越以胤為冠軍將軍、南陽太守。

translations.literal: Yue appointed Yin champion general, prefect of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yue then named Yin champion general and governor of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 胤從藍田出武關，之南陽，前守衛展距胤不受，胤乃還洛。

translations.literal: Yin exited from Lantian through Wu Pass, went to Nanyang; the former defender Wei Zhan resisted Yin and would not accept him; Yin then returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yin marched from Lantian through Wu Pass toward Nanyang, but the sitting governor Wei Zhan barred him; he had to withdraw to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 懷帝即位，拜胤左衛將軍，轉散騎常侍、太僕卿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended, Yin was appointed general of the left guard, transferred cavalier attendant in regular attendance, minister coachman.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Huai he became general of the left guard, then cavalier attendant in regular attendance and minister coachman.

sentences.zh: 既而與播及帝舅王延、尚書何綏、太史令高堂沖並參機密，為東海王越所害。

translations.literal: Subsequently together with Bo and the emperor’s maternal uncle Wang Yan, minister He Sui, grand astrologer Gao Tang Chong he participated in secret matters, and was killed by Prince of Donghai Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Bo, the emperor’s uncle Wang Yan, He Sui, and Gao Tang Chong in Huai’s inner council until Sima Yue murdered them all.

sentences.zh: 皇甫重

translations.literal: Huangfu Chong
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Chong

sentences.zh: 皇甫重，字倫叔，安定朝那人也。

translations.literal: Huangfu Chong, courtesy name Lundshu, was a man of Chaona in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Chong, courtesy Lundshu, came from Chaona in Anding commandery.

sentences.zh: 性沈果，有才用，為司空張華所知，稍遷新平太守。

translations.literal: His nature was deep and resolute; he had talent and utility; was known to minister of works Zhang Hua, gradually promoted prefect of Xinping.
translations.idiomatic: Grave, decisive, and capable, he came to Zhang Hua’s notice and rose to prefect of Xinping.

sentences.zh: 元康中，華版為秦州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Yuankang era Hua by ad hoc appointment made him inspector of Qin province.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuankang, Zhang Hua issued an extraordinary commission making him inspector of Qin.

sentences.zh: 齊王冏輔政，以重弟商為參軍。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qi Sima Jiong assisted governance, he made Chong’s younger brother Shang a staff recorder.
translations.idiomatic: While Sima Jiong of Qi directed the government, he took Chong’s brother Shang onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 冏誅，長沙王乂又以為參軍。

translations.literal: When Jiong was executed, Prince Changsha Sima Yi again made [Shang] a staff recorder.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiong fell, Sima Yi of Changsha likewise employed Shang as recorder.

sentences.zh: 時河間王顒鎮關中，其將李含先與商、重有隙，每銜之，及此，說顒曰：「商為乂所任，重終不為人用，宜急除之，以去一方之患。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Hejian Sima Yong guarded Guanzhong; his general Li Han had earlier had a rift with Shang and Chong, always bore resentment against them; reaching this point, he said to Yong, “Shang is employed by Yi; Chong in the end will not be used by you—should urgently eliminate them to remove a region’s calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yong of Hejian held the northwest while his general Li Han, who had long hated the brothers, whispered: “Shang serves Sima Yi; Chong will never be yours—cut them down now or the west will burn.”

sentences.zh: 可表遷重為內職，因其經長安，乃執之。

translations.literal: ” One can memorialize promoting Chong to an inner post; when he passes through Chang’an on the route, then seize him.
translations.idiomatic: “Memorialize a transfer for Chong to a capital post and arrest him when he passes through Chang’an.”

sentences.zh: 」重知其謀，乃露檄上尚書，以顒信任李含，將欲為亂，召集隴上士眾，以討含為名。

translations.literal: ” Chong knew their plot; thereupon he exposed a public dispatch to the ministry of appointments, charging that Yong trusted Li Han and was about to bring chaos; he gathered hosts on Long and raised troops in the name of punishing Han.
translations.idiomatic: Chong learned of the ruse, published a manifesto to the ministry accusing Yong and Li Han of treason, and mobilized the Long plateau gentry in a punitive march against Han.

sentences.zh: 乂以兵革累興，今始寧息，表請遣使詔重罷兵，徵含為河南尹。

translations.literal: Yi because weapons and armor had repeatedly risen and now first had quieted, memorialized requesting dispatch of envoys to proclaim an edict ordering Chong to cease troops and summon Han as prefect of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi, eager to stop another civil war, asked the court to send envoys ordering Chong to stand down while summoning Li Han to the Henan prefecture—hoping to separate the conspirators.

sentences.zh: 含既就徵，重不奉詔，顒遣金城太守游楷、隴西太守韓稚等四郡兵攻之。

translations.literal: When Han had answered the summons, Chong did not obey the edict; Yong sent Jinshang prefect You Kai, Longxi prefect Han Zhi, and troops of four commanderies to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han obeyed and went east, yet Chong refused the edict; Yong answered by flinging four commandery armies under You Kai and Han Zhi against his city.

sentences.zh: 頃之，成都王穎與顒起兵共攻乂，以討-{后}-父尚書僕射羊玄之及商為名。

translations.literal: Shortly Prince of Chengdu Sima Ying with Yong raised troops together to attack Yi, in the name of punishing Empress Yang’s father, grand master of the works Yang Xuanzhi, and Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Sima Ying of Chengdu joined Yong in a march against Sima Yi, claiming they meant to punish Empress Yang’s father, Yang Xuanzhi, and Huangfu Shang.

sentences.zh: 乂以商為左將軍、河東太守，領萬餘人于關門距張方，為方所破，顒軍遂進。

translations.literal: Yi appointed Shang general of the left, prefect of Hedong, leading more than ten thousand men at the pass gate to resist Zhang Fang; he was broken by Fang, and Yong’s army then advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Yi named Shang general of the left and governor of Hedong, sent him with ten thousand men to hold the pass against Zhang Fang, lost the battle, and opened the road for Yong’s host.

sentences.zh: 乂既屢敗，乃使商間行齎帝手詔，使遊楷盡罷兵，令重進軍討顒。

translations.literal: Yi having repeatedly been defeated, then sent Shang by secret route carrying the emperor’s autograph edict, ordering You Kai entirely to dismiss troops and ordering Chong to advance forces to punish Yong.
translations.idiomatic: After further defeats Yi smuggled an autograph edict to Shang instructing You Kai to disengage and ordering Chong to turn his guns on Yong.

sentences.zh: 商行過長安，至新平，遇其從甥，從甥素憎商，以告顒，顒捕得商，殺之。

translations.literal: Shang’s route passed Chang’an, reached Xinping, met his cousin by the mother’s side; the cousin had long hated Shang, informed Yong; Yong captured Shang and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shang slipped past Chang’an to Xinping, where a cousin who despised him betrayed him to Yong; Yong seized and executed him.

sentences.zh: 乂既敗，重猶堅守，閉塞外門，城內莫知，而四郡兵築土山攻城，重輒以連弩射之。

translations.literal: Yi having been defeated, Chong still firmly defended, blocking the outer gate; inside the city none knew [the news]; yet four-commandery troops built earthen hills to attack the city; Chong always shot them with linked crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: Even after Yi’s fall Chong held his walls, sealed the outer gates so no news leaked in, and raked the besiegers’ siege mounds with repeating crossbows.

sentences.zh: 所在為地窟以防外攻，權變百端，外軍不得近城，將士為之死戰。

translations.literal: Everywhere they dug tunnels against outside attack; stratagems changed a hundred ways; outer armies could not approach the city; officers and soldiers for him fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: His men burrowed countermines, shifted tactics endlessly, and kept the outer lines from closing until every soldier fought as if it were his last day.

sentences.zh: 顒知不可拔，乃上表求遣御史宣詔喻之令降。

translations.literal: Yong knew it could not be taken; thereupon he submitted a memorial requesting dispatch of censors to proclaim the edict instructing him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the siege stall, Yong asked Luoyang to send censors with an edict promising Chong safe surrender.

sentences.zh: 重知非朝廷本意，不奉詔。

translations.literal: Chong knew it was not the original intent of the court and did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Chong saw through the ploy as Yong’s, not the emperor’s, and ignored the summons.

sentences.zh: 獲御史騶人問曰：「我弟將兵來，欲至未？

translations.literal: Capturing the censor’s groom he asked, “My younger brother leading troops—is he about to arrive yet?
translations.idiomatic: He seized a herald from the escort and demanded, “Is my brother’s relief column close?”

sentences.zh: 」騶云：「已為河間王所害。

translations.literal: ” The groom said, “Already killed by Prince of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: The man answered, “Prince Yong has already killed him.”

sentences.zh: 」重失色，立殺騶。

translations.literal: ” Chong changed color and immediately killed the groom.
translations.idiomatic: Chong went white with rage and slew the messenger on the spot.

sentences.zh: 於是城內知無外救，遂共殺重。

translations.literal: Thereupon those inside the city knew there was no outside relief; together they killed Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Once the garrison knew no help was coming, they turned on Chong and cut him down.

sentences.zh: 先是，重被圍急，遣養子昌請救于東海王越，越以顒新廢成都王穎，與山東連和，不肯出兵。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chong was besieged tight, he sent foster son Chang to beg rescue from Prince of Donghai Yue; Yue because Yong had newly deposed Prince of Chengdu Ying and allied with Shandong, was unwilling to send troops.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, under tight siege, Chong’s adopted son Chang had begged Sima Yue for troops; Yue, who had just reconciled with Yong after deposing Ying, refused to march.

sentences.zh: 昌乃與故殿中人楊篇詐稱越命，迎羊-{后}-於金墉城入宮，以后令發兵討張方，奉迎大駕。

translations.literal: Chang then with former palace insider Yang Pian falsely claimed Yue’s order, welcomed Empress Yang from the Golden Moat bastion into the palace, using the empress’s order to raise troops against Zhang Fang and escort the great chariot.
translations.idiomatic: Chang then forged Yue’s orders with palace agent Yang Pian, freed Empress Yang from Jinyong fortress, and tried to mobilize the capital against Zhang Fang in the emperor’s name.

sentences.zh: 事起倉卒，百官初皆從之，俄而又共誅昌。

translations.literal: The affair arose in haste; all hundred officials at first followed it; shortly afterward they together executed Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Officials briefly followed the coup, then sobered up and executed Chang.

sentences.zh: 張輔

translations.literal: Zhang Fu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu

sentences.zh: 張輔，字世偉，南陽西鄂人，漢河間相衡之後也。

translations.literal: Zhang Fu, courtesy name Shiwei, was a man of Xi’e in Nanyang, a descendant of Han’s Hejian chancellor Zhang Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fu, courtesy Shiwei, came from Xi’e in Nanyang and traced his line to the Han minister Zhang Heng, who had served as chancellor of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 少有幹局，與從母兄劉喬齊名。

translations.literal: In youth he had capacity for administration; with elder maternal cousin Liu Qiao he shared fame.
translations.idiomatic: He showed administrative talent early and was reckoned the equal of his elder cousin Liu Qiao.

sentences.zh: 初補藍田令，不為豪強所屈。

translations.literal: First he was supplemented as magistrate of Lantian and was not bent by magnates.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Lantian he refused to bend before local magnates.

sentences.zh: 時強弩將軍龐宗，西州大姓，護軍趙浚，宗婦族也，故僮僕放縱，為百姓所患。

translations.literal: At that time sturdy-crossbow general Pang Zong was a great clan of the western province; protector Zhao Jun was kin of Zong’s wife’s clan, so slaves and servants ran wild and were a calamity to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: The general Pang Zong, a western magnate, let his in-laws—protector Zhao Jun among them—terrorize the district with armed retainers.

sentences.zh: 輔繩之，殺其二奴，又奪宗田二百餘頃以給貧戶，一縣稱之。

translations.literal: Fu applied law to them, killed two of Zong’s slaves, and seized over two hundred qing of Zong’s fields to give to poor households; the whole county praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu enforced the statute, executed two of Pang’s slaves, confiscated more than two hundred qing of clan land for the destitute, and won the county’s praise.

sentences.zh: 轉山陽令，太尉陳准家僮亦暴橫，輔復擊殺之。

translations.literal: Transferred magistrate of Shanyang—Grand Commandant Chen Zhun’s household servants were also violent and overbearing; Fu again struck and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Shanyang, he likewise beat Chen Zhun’s swaggering housemen to death.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書郎，封宜昌亭侯。

translations.literal: He ascended to gentleman of the ministries, was enfeoffed village marquis of Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to ministry gentleman and village marquis of Yichang.

sentences.zh: 轉御史中丞。

translations.literal: Transferred palace secretary in charge of law.
translations.idiomatic: Next he became imperial secretary.

sentences.zh: 時積弩將軍孟觀與明威將軍郝彥不協，而觀因軍事害彥，又賈謐、潘岳、石崇等共相引重，乃義陽王威有詐冒事，輔並糾劾之。

translations.literal: At that time rapid-crossbow general Meng Guan and general who displays might Hao Yan were not harmonious, and Guan through military affairs harmed Yan; also Jia Mi, Pan Yue, Shi Chong and others mutually promoted each other; moreover Prince of Yiyang Sima Wei had a fraud matter—Fu together impeached them all.
translations.idiomatic: While Meng Guan used his command to ruin rival Hao Yan, Jia Mi, Pan Yue, and Shi Chong built a mutual praise ring, and Prince Sima Wei of Yiyang faced fraud charges—Fu impeached the whole pack.

sentences.zh: 梁州刺史楊欣有姊喪，未經旬，車騎長史韓預強聘其女為妻。

translations.literal: Inspector of Liang Yang Xin had an elder sister’s mourning, not yet a full ten days, when chariot-and-horse chief clerk Han Yu forcibly engaged his daughter as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Liang inspector Yang Xin was still mourning his sister when chief clerk Han Yu tried to seize his daughter for a forced marriage within ten days of the death.

sentences.zh: 輔為中正，貶預以清風俗，論者稱之。

translations.literal: Fu as local evaluator demoted Yu to clarify customs; discussers praised him.
translations.idiomatic: As regional appraiser Fu demoted Han to set a moral example, and opinion applauded him.

sentences.zh: 用孫秀執權，威構輔於秀，秀惑之，將繩輔以法。

translations.literal: Because Sun Xiu seized power, Wei framed Fu to Xiu; Xiu was deluded and was about to bind Fu by law.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sun Xiu dominated the court, Sima Wei slandered Fu; Sun almost had him indicted.

sentences.zh: 輔與秀箋曰：「輔徒知希慕古人，當官而行，不復自知小為身計。

translations.literal: Fu wrote to Xiu, saying, “Fu only knows to admire the ancients and, on taking office, to act, no longer aware in small measure of calculating for the self.
translations.idiomatic: Fu wrote Sun Xiu: “I have only tried to imitate the ancients—do the job, not count the cost to myself.”

sentences.zh: 今義陽王誠弘恕，不以介意。

translations.literal: ” Now Prince of Yiyang is truly magnanimous and does not mind it.
translations.idiomatic: “Prince Wei of Yiyang has already forgiven the affair.”

sentences.zh: 然輔母年七十六，常見憂慮，恐輔將以怨疾獲罪。

translations.literal: ” Yet Fu’s mother is seventy-six sui and often shows worry and anxiety; I fear Fu will on account of resentment and illness incur guilt.
translations.idiomatic: “But my mother is seventy-six and sick with worry that spite will destroy me.”

sentences.zh: 願明公留神省察輔前後行事，是國之愚臣而已。

translations.literal: ” I hope the enlightened lord will attend and examine Fu’s conduct before and after—only the state’s foolish minister, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: “I beg you to review my record—I am merely a clumsy servant of the law.”

sentences.zh: 「秀雖凶狡，知輔雅正，為威所誣，乃止。

translations.literal: ” Xiu though fierce and cunning knew Fu was upright and classical, was slandered by Wei, and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiu, vicious as he was, recognized Fu’s integrity, saw through Wei’s malice, and dropped the case.

sentences.zh: 後遷馮翊太守。

translations.literal: Later promoted prefect of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to prefect of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 是時長沙王乂以河間王顒專制關中，有不臣之跡，言于惠帝，密詔雍州刺史劉沈、秦州刺史皇甫重使討顒。

translations.literal: At this time Prince Changsha Sima Yi because Prince of Hejian Yong monopolized Guanzhong with traces of disloyalty, spoke to Emperor Hui, who secretly ordered inspector of Yong Liu Shen and inspector of Qin Huangfu Chong to campaign against Yong.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yi of Changsha concluded that Yong was ruling Guanzhong like a separatist, he persuaded Emperor Hui to issue secret orders for Liu Shen and Huangfu Chong to strike him.

sentences.zh: 於是沈等與顒戰于長安，輔遂將兵救顒，沈等敗績。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shen and others fought Yong at Chang’an; Fu thereupon led troops to rescue Yong; Shen and others were routed.
translations.idiomatic: Battle flared at Chang’an; Zhang Fu marched to Yong’s relief and shattered Liu Shen’s host.

sentences.zh: 顒德之，乃以輔代重為秦州刺史。

translations.literal: Yong was grateful and therefore appointed Fu to replace Chong as inspector of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful, Yong replaced Huangfu Chong with Zhang Fu as inspector of Qin.

sentences.zh: 當赴顒之難，金城太守游楷亦皆有功，轉梁州刺史，不之官。

translations.literal: When he was answering Yong’s crisis, Jinshang prefect You Kai also all had merit, was transferred inspector of Liang, but did not go to office.
translations.idiomatic: You Kai of Jinshang had earned merit in the same crisis and was named inspector of Liang, though he never took up the post.

sentences.zh: 楷聞輔之還，不時迎輔，陰圖之。

translations.literal: When Kai heard Fu was returning, he did not promptly welcome Fu and secretly plotted against him.
translations.idiomatic: You Kai, learning that Fu was coming west, delayed his reception and schemed against him.

sentences.zh: 又殺天水太守封尚，欲揚威西土。

translations.literal: He also killed Tian prefect of Tianshui Feng Shang, wishing to display might in the western lands.
translations.idiomatic: He murdered Feng Shang, the prefect of Tianshui, to cow the northwest.

sentences.zh: 召隴西太守韓稚會議，未決。

translations.literal: He summoned Longxi prefect Han Zhi to council; they did not decide.
translations.idiomatic: He called Longxi governor Han Zhi to council, but they could not agree.

sentences.zh: 稚子朴有武幹，斬異議者，即收兵伐輔。

translations.literal: Zhi’s son Pu had martial efficiency, beheaded those who disagreed, immediately collected troops to attack Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zhi’s son Pu had military grit; he executed the waverers and mobilized troops against Fu.

sentences.zh: 輔與稚戰于遮多穀口，輔軍敗績，為天水故帳下督富整所殺。

translations.literal: Fu fought Zhi at Zheduo Valley mouth; Fu’s army was routed; he was killed by Fu Zheng, former chief of tent staff at Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: The armies met at Zhedu Gorge; Fu lost, and Fu Zheng, once a household captain in Tianshui, struck off his head.

sentences.zh: 初，輔嘗著論云：「管仲不若鮑叔，鮑叔知所奉，知所投。

translations.literal: Earlier Fu had once composed a treatise saying, “Guan Zhong is not equal to Bao Shuu; Bao Shuu knew whom to serve and whom to join.
translations.idiomatic: Fu once argued in an essay that Guan Zhong fell short of Bao Shuu because Bao knew whom to serve and when to change sides.

sentences.zh: 管仲奉主而不能濟，所奔又非濟事之國，三歸反坫，皆鮑不為。

translations.literal: ” Guan Zhong served a lord but could not save him; what he fled to was again not a state able to save the affair; three returns and inverted cup-stand—all Bao did not do.
translations.idiomatic: “Guan served a doomed liege, fled to courts that could not save the realm, and flaunted the luxuries Bao Shuu never touched.”

sentences.zh: 」又論班固、司馬遷云：「遷之著述，辭約而事舉，敘三千年事唯五十萬言；

translations.literal: ” Also he discussed Ban Gu and Sima Qian, saying, “Qian’s writing, diction tight while events are raised, narrating three thousand years’ affairs in only five hundred thousand words;
translations.idiomatic: He also compared Ban Gu with Sima Qian: “Qian’s prose is spare yet covers three millennia in half a million graphs;

sentences.zh: 班固敘二百年事乃八十萬言，煩省不同，不如遷一也。

translations.literal: Ban Gu narrates two hundred years’ affairs and yet eight hundred thousand words—the tedious and concise are not the same; Gu is not equal to Qian by one point.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu needs eight hundred thousand graphs for two centuries—one is prolix, the other lean; Ban trails by a wide margin.”

sentences.zh: 良史述事，善足以獎勸，惡足以監誡，人道之常。

translations.literal: A good historian narrates affairs: good is enough to encourage, evil enough to warn and admonish—this is the constant of human relations.
translations.idiomatic: A worthy historian praises enough to inspire and censures enough to warn—that is the moral office of history.”

sentences.zh: 中流小事，亦無取焉，而班皆書之，不如二也。

translations.literal: Middle-stream small matters he also records without selection—Ban writes them all—not equal to Qian, second point.
translations.idiomatic: Ban pads his annals with trivia Qian would have dropped—that is a second way he falls short.

sentences.zh: 毀貶晁錯，傷忠臣之道，不如三也。

translations.literal: He slanders and demotes Chao Cuo, injuring the way of loyal ministers—not equal, third point.
translations.idiomatic: He vilifies Chao Cuo and betrays the ethic of loyal ministers—that is a third failing.

sentences.zh: 遷既造創，固又因循，難易益不同矣。

translations.literal: Qian first created the form; Ban merely followed along—the difficulty and ease are moreover not the same.
translations.idiomatic: Qian invented the Grand Scribe’s form while Ban only inherited it; their labors were not comparable.

sentences.zh: 又遷為蘇秦、張儀、范睢、蔡澤作傳，逞辭流離，亦足以明其大才。

translations.literal: Moreover Qian wrote biographies for Su Qin, Zhang Yi, Fan Ju, and Cai Ze, letting rhetoric run and wander, also sufficient to display their great talent.
translations.idiomatic: Qian’s chapters on Su Qin, Zhang Yi, Fan Ju, and Cai Ze let rhetorical brilliance run free—enough to show genius at work.

sentences.zh: 故述辯士則辭藻華靡，敘實錄則隱核名檢，此所以遷稱良史也。

translations.literal: Therefore when narrating debaters the phrasing is ornate; when narrating true records he is hidden yet exact in names and norms—this is why Qian is called a good historian.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian writes persuaders his prose dazzles; when he records fact he is spare and exact—hence historians call him a master.

sentences.zh: 」又論魏武帝不及劉備，樂毅減於諸葛亮，詞多不載。

translations.literal: ” He also argued that Wei Wu-di did not match Liu Bei and Yue Yi fell short of Zhuge Liang—most of the wording is not preserved here.
translations.idiomatic: He likewise ranked Cao Cao below Liu Bei and Yue Yi below Zhuge Liang; the full text is too long to quote.

sentences.zh: 李含

translations.literal: Li Han
translations.idiomatic: Li Han

sentences.zh: 李含，字世容，隴西狄道人也。

translations.literal: Li Han, courtesy name Shirong, was a man of Didao in Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han, courtesy Shirong, came from Didao in Longxi commandery.

sentences.zh: 僑居始平。

translations.literal: He sojourned in Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: His family had settled in Shiping.

sentences.zh: 少有才幹，兩郡並舉孝廉。

translations.literal: In youth he had talent and capacity; two commanderies together recommended him filial and incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Young Li Han showed administrative promise and won simultaneous filial-and-incorrupt nominations from two prefectures.

sentences.zh: 安定皇甫商州裏年少，少恃豪族，以含門寒微，欲與結交，含距而不納，商恨焉，遂諷州以短檄召含為門亭長。

translations.literal: Huangfu Shang of Anding, a young man of the district, relying on a powerful clan, because Han’s gate was cold and humble wished to befriend him; Han refused and would not accept; Shang resented it, therefore induced the province with a short dispatch to summon Han as chief of the gate pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Shang, a swaggering local magnate from Anding, offered friendship; Li Han, scorning his pedigree, rebuffed him, so Shang had the province appoint Han petty warden of the gate—public humiliation.

sentences.zh: 會州刺史郭奕素聞其賢，下車擢含為別駕，遂處群僚之右。

translations.literal: It happened that Inspector Guo Yi had long heard of his worth; dismounting from the carriage he promoted Han to aide-de-camp, and he then stood to the right of the host of officials.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Guo Yi, who had long admired Han, raised him straight to chief clerk, placing him above the rest of the staff.

sentences.zh: 尋舉秀才，薦之公府，自太保掾轉秦國郎中令。

translations.literal: Shortly he was raised cultivated talent and recommended to the excellencies’ offices; from grand tutor’s clerk he was transferred minister of the princedom of Qin’s gentleman in charge of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He soon passed the cultivated-talent exam, entered the central offices, and moved from clerk to the grand tutor into the household ministry of the Qin princedom.

sentences.zh: 司徒遷含領始平中正。

translations.literal: The minister of education transferred Han to head the Shiping local evaluator.
translations.idiomatic: The minister of education named him chief appraiser for Shiping.

sentences.zh: 秦王柬薨，含依臺儀，葬訖除喪。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qin Sima Jian died, Han according to court ritual, after burial completed, doffed mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Qin Sima Jian died, Li Han ended mourning on schedule per board regulations.

sentences.zh: 尚書趙浚有內寵，疾含不事己，遂奏含不應除喪。

translations.literal: Minister Zhao Jun had inner favor; he hated Han for not serving himself; thereupon he memorialized that Han ought not to have doffed mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhao Jun, a palace favorite, hated Han for ignoring him and impeached him for leaving mourning early.

sentences.zh: 本州大中正傅祗以名義貶含。

translations.literal: The great local evaluator of the province Fu Di degraded Han on grounds of propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial grand appraiser Fu Di struck his name from the rolls for violating ritual.

sentences.zh: 中丞傅咸上表理含曰：

translations.literal: Palace secretary in charge of law Fu Xian submitted a memorial arguing for Han, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Imperial secretary Fu Xian sent up a long memorial defending Li Han:

sentences.zh: 帝不從，含遂被貶，退割為五品。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow; Han was therefore demoted, degraded by rank-cut to fifth grade.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ignored Fu Xian; Han was stripped to fifth-rank status.

sentences.zh: 歸長安，歲餘，光祿差含為壽城邸閣督。

translations.literal: He returned to Chang’an; after more than a year the household grandee’s office assigned Han as overseer of the Shoucheng lodge gate.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Chang’an a year later, the household grandee parked him as warden of the Shoucheng hostel.

sentences.zh: 司徒王戎表含曾為大臣，雖見割削，不應降為此職。

translations.literal: Minister of education Wang Rong memorialized that Han had once been a great minister; though he had seen rank-cut, he ought not be lowered to this office.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong protested: a man who had served as a senior minister should not be parked at a porter’s post.

sentences.zh: 詔停。

translations.literal: An edict halted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stayed the demotion.

sentences.zh: 後為始平令。

translations.literal: Later he became magistrate of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: He was later restored as magistrate of Shiping.

sentences.zh: 及趙王倫篡位，或謂孫秀曰：「李含有文武大才，無以資人。

translations.literal: When King of Zhao Sima Lun usurped, someone said to Sun Xiu, “Li Han has great civil and military talent yet stands without a patron to back him.
translations.idiomatic: During Lun’s coup someone told Sun Xiu, “Li Han is brilliant in civil and military affairs but lacks powerful friends—

sentences.zh: 」秀以為東武陽令。

translations.literal: ” Xiu made him magistrate of Dongwuyang.
translations.idiomatic: you can win him cheaply.” Sun Xiu named him magistrate of Dongwuyang.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒表請含為征西司馬，甚見信任。

translations.literal: Prince of Hejian Yong memorialized requesting Han as western expedition marshal; he was greatly trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yong then took him west as expedition marshal and trusted every word he spoke.

sentences.zh: 頃之，轉為長史。

translations.literal: Shortly he was transferred chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he rose to chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 顒誅夏侯奭，送齊王冏使與趙王倫，遣張方率眾赴倫，皆含謀也。

translations.literal: Yong executed Xiahou Shi, sent Prince of Qi Jiong to King of Zhao Lun, dispatched Zhang Fang leading a host to go to Lun—all were Han’s stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Yong’s execution of Xiahou Shi, his shipment of Sima Jiong to Sima Lun, and Zhang Fang’s march east were all Li Han’s plots.

sentences.zh: 後顒聞三王兵盛，乃加含龍驤將軍，統席薳等鐵騎，回遣張方軍以應義師。

translations.literal: Later Yong heard the three kings’ troops were strong; thereupon he added Han dragon-soaring general, commanding Xi Sui and others’ armored cavalry, turning Zhang Fang’s army to answer the righteous hosts.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied princes grew formidable, Yong gave Han the dragon-soaring banner, iron cavalry under Xi Sui, and ordered Zhang Fang to swing about and join the loyalists.

sentences.zh: 天子反正，含至潼關而還。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven returned to rectitude, Han reached Tong Pass and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor was restored, Li Han marched only as far as Tong Pass before Yong recalled him.

sentences.zh: 初，梁州刺史皇甫商為趙王倫所任，倫敗，去職詣顒，顒慰撫之甚厚。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liang inspector Huangfu Shang had been employed by King of Zhao Lun; when Lun failed, [Shang] left office and went to Yong; Yong consoled and treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Liang inspector Huangfu Shang had served Sima Lun; after Lun’s fall he fled to Yong, who welcomed him like an old friend.

sentences.zh: 含諫顒曰：「商，倫之信臣，懼罪至此，不宜數與相見。

translations.literal: Han remonstrated with Yong, saying, “Shang is Lun’s trusted minister; fearing guilt he has come here—it is not fitting repeatedly to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han warned Yong: “Shang was Lun’s intimate; he comes in fear, not friendship—do not court him openly.”

sentences.zh: 」商知而恨之。

translations.literal: ” Shang knew it and resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Shang learned of the slight and hated Han.

sentences.zh: 及商當還都，顒置酒餞行，商因與含忿爭，顒和釋之。

translations.literal: When Shang was about to return to the capital, Yong set wine to see him off; Shang therefore quarreled angrily with Han; Yong reconciled them.
translations.idiomatic: At Shang’s farewell banquet the two men nearly came to blows until Yong separated them.

sentences.zh: 後含被徵為翊軍校尉。

translations.literal: Later Han was summoned as colonel of the guards who aid [the army].
translations.idiomatic: Later the court summoned Han as colonel of the assisting guards.

sentences.zh: 時商參齊王冏軍事，而夏侯奭兄在冏府，稱奭立義，被西籓枉害。

translations.literal: At that time Shang was participating in Prince of Qi Jiong’s military affairs, while Xiahou Shi’s elder brother was in Jiong’s office, claiming Shi had raised righteousness and was wrongly harmed by the western vassal.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Shang sat on Sima Jiong’s staff while Xiahou Shi’s brother petitioned that Shi had died a loyal martyr at Yong’s hands.

sentences.zh: 含心不自安。

translations.literal: Han’s heart was not at ease within.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han saw the trap closing and could not sleep.

sentences.zh: 冏右司馬趙驤又與含有隙，冏將閱武，含懼驤因兵討之，乃單馬出奔於顒，矯稱受密詔。

translations.literal: Jiong’s right marshal Zhao Xiang again had a rift with Han; Jiong was about to review troops; Han feared Xiang would use troops to punish him; thereupon on a single horse he fled out to Yong, falsely claiming he had received a secret edict.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong’s right marshal Zhao Xiang also despised him; when Jiong scheduled a military review, Han bolted to Yong’s camp claiming he carried a secret edict.

sentences.zh: 顒即夜見之，乃說顒曰：「成都王至親，有大功，還籓，甚得眾心。

translations.literal: Yong immediately received him by night; thereupon he persuaded Yong, saying, “Prince of Chengdu is closest kin, has great merit, returned to his fief—he greatly wins the people’s hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Yong admitted him by torchlight; Han whispered: “Sima Ying is the emperor’s closest kinsman, a proven champion sent home to his fief—he still commands love in the army.

sentences.zh: 齊王越親而專執威權，朝廷側目。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi is closer yet monopolizes awing power; the court sideways-eyes him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jiong, nearer the throne, hoards every spear; the whole court glares at him.

sentences.zh: 今檄長沙王令討齊，使先聞于齊，齊必誅長沙，因傳檄以加齊罪，則冏可擒也。

translations.literal: Now dispatch a call ordering Prince Changsha Yi to punish Qi; first let Qi hear of it; Qi will surely execute Changsha; then propagate a call to add Qi’s crimes—then Jiong can be seized.
translations.idiomatic: Issue an edict telling Sima Yi to strike Jiong; leak word so Jiong murders Yi first, then publish Jiong’s crimes—Jiong will fall into your net.

sentences.zh: 既去齊，立成都，除逼建親，以安社稷，大勳也。

translations.literal: Once Qi is removed, establish Prince of Chengdu, eliminate oppression and establish kin—thereby to secure the altars of soil and grain—this is a great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Cut Jiong away, elevate Ying, break the choke hold and bind the family to the throne—that would be a deed for the ages.”

sentences.zh: 」顒從之，遂表請討冏，拜含為都督，統張方等率諸軍以向洛陽。

translations.literal: ” Yong followed it; thereupon he submitted a memorial requesting to punish Jiong, appointed Han area commander, commanding Zhang Fang and others leading the various hosts toward Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yong agreed, memorialized for war on Jiong, and named Han supreme commander with Zhang Fang’s legions rolling toward Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 含屯陰盤，而長沙王乂誅冏，含等旋師。

translations.literal: Han encamped at Yinpan, but Prince Changsha Yi executed Jiong; Han and others wheeled the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Han camped at Yinpan, but Sima Yi killed Jiong before the blow landed, so the western army marched home.

sentences.zh: 初，含之本謀欲並去乂、冏，使權歸於顒，含因得肆其宿志。

translations.literal: Earlier, Han’s original plan wished simultaneously to remove Yi and Jiong, so that power would return to Yong, and Han thereby could indulge his long-held aims.
translations.idiomatic: Han’s deeper design had been to destroy both Yi and Jiong so Yong—and Han—could seize the government.

sentences.zh: 既長沙勝齊，顒、穎猶各守籓，志望未允。

translations.literal: Already Changsha defeated Qi, yet Yong and Ying still each guarded their fiefs; aims and hopes were not fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: With Jiong dead but Yi alive, Yong and Ying stayed bottled in their domains—Han’s ambitions stalled.

sentences.zh: 顒表含為河南尹。

translations.literal: Yong memorialized Han as prefect of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yong then appointed him prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 時商復被乂任遇，商兄重時為秦州刺史，含疾商滋甚，復與重構隙。
