translations.literal: At that time Shang again received Yi’s favor; Shang’s elder brother Chong was then inspector of Qin province; Han’s illness toward Shang grew worse, and again he constructed a rift with Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Shang resurfaced as Yi’s favorite while his brother Chong held Qin; Li Han’s hatred doubled, and he turned Chong against Yong.

sentences.zh: 顒自含奔還之後，委以心膂，復慮重襲己，乃使兵圍之，更相表罪。

translations.literal: Yong since Han’s flight back had entrusted him as backbone and heart, yet also feared Chong would strike himself; thereupon he sent troops to besiege him; each side sent up memorials accusing the other’s crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Yong, who had staked everything on Han, now feared Chong would attack him first, besieged Chong’s city, and traded accusations with Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 侍中馮蓀黨顒，請召重還。

translations.literal: Palace attendant Feng Sun sided with Yong and requested summoning Chong back.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Feng Sun, Yong’s partisan, urged the court to recall Chong.

sentences.zh: 商說乂曰：「河間之奏，皆李含所交構也。

translations.literal: Shang persuaded Yi, saying, “Hejian’s memorials are all woven by Li Han’s scheming.
translations.idiomatic: Shang told Yi: “Every petition from Yong is Li Han’s poison pen.

sentences.zh: 若不早圖，禍將至矣。

translations.literal: If you do not plan early, calamity will arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Move before he moves or you will burn.”

sentences.zh: 且河間前舉，由含之謀。

translations.literal: Moreover Hejian’s earlier rising came from Han’s stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Remember: Yong’s first eastern march was Han’s idea.”

sentences.zh: 」乂乃殺含。

translations.literal: ” Yi then killed Han.
translations.idiomatic: Yi believed him and executed Li Han.

sentences.zh: 張方

translations.literal: Zhang Fang
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fang

sentences.zh: 張方，河間人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Fang was a man of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fang came from the Hejian princedom.

sentences.zh: 世貧賤，以材勇得幸于河間王顒，累遷兼振武將軍。

translations.literal: For generations poor and lowly, by talent and bravery he won favor with Prince of Hejian Yong, ascending to concurrent general who shakes might.
translations.idiomatic: Born poor, he won Sima Yong’s trust through sheer nerve and rose to concurrent general who shakes might.

sentences.zh: 永寧中，顒表討齊王冏，遣方領兵二萬為前鋒。

translations.literal: In the Yongning era Yong memorialized to punish Prince of Qi Jiong, dispatching Fang to lead twenty thousand troops as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongning Yong sent Fang east with twenty thousand van-guards against Sima Jiong.

sentences.zh: 及冏被長沙王乂所殺，顒及成都王穎復表討乂，遣方率眾自函谷人屯河南。

translations.literal: When Jiong was killed by Prince Changsha Yi, Yong and Prince of Chengdu Ying again memorialized to punish Yi, dispatching Fang leading a host from Hangu Pass to enter and encamp south of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiong fell to Sima Yi, Yong and Sima Ying renewed the war and ordered Fang through Hangu into Henan.

sentences.zh: 惠帝遣左將軍皇甫商距之，方以潛軍破商之眾，遂入城。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui dispatched General of the Left Huangfu Shang to resist him; Fang with a concealed army broke Shang’s host, thereupon entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui sent Huangfu Shang to hold the line; Fang ambushed him and stormed Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 乂奉帝討方於城內，方軍望見乘輿，於是小退，方止之不得，眾遂大敗，殺傷滿於衢巷。

translations.literal: Yi upheld the emperor to punish Fang inside the city; Fang’s army caught sight of the imperial carriage and therefore slightly withdrew; Fang could not stop them; the host was greatly defeated, killing and wounding filled the lanes.
translations.idiomatic: Yi rode out with the emperor; Fang’s men faltered at the sight of the imperial carriage, routed in the alleys in a bloodbath.

sentences.zh: 方退壁於十三里橋，人情挫衄，無復固志，多勸方夜遁。

translations.literal: Fang withdrew to fortify at the Thirteen-Li Bridge; morale was crushed and snagged, no longer firm in resolve; many urged Fang to flee by night.
translations.idiomatic: Fang fell back to the Thirteen-Li Bridge, where shattered morale nearly drove him to a midnight retreat.

sentences.zh: 方曰：「兵之利鈍是常，貴因敗以為成耳。

translations.literal: Fang said, “Sharpness and dullness of arms are constant; what is precious is to turn defeat into success.
translations.idiomatic: Fang barked, “Armies win and lose—that is normal; genius lies in turning rout into victory.”

sentences.zh: 我更前作壘，出其不意，此用兵之奇也。

translations.literal: ” I will advance again and build ramparts, catching them unprepared—this is the oddity of using troops.
translations.idiomatic: “We will creep closer, throw up new walls, and strike before they recover—that is how you steal a war.”

sentences.zh: 」乃夜潛進逼洛城七里。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon by night he secretly advanced pressing Luoyang within seven li.
translations.idiomatic: That night he slipped within seven li of the walls.

sentences.zh: 乂既新捷，不以為意，忽聞方壘成，乃出戰，敗績。

translations.literal: Yi having newly won victory, did not take it to heart; suddenly hearing Fang’s ramparts were complete, then went out to battle and was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, drunk on his recent win, ignored the threat until Fang’s new camp rose; he sallied forth and lost everything.

sentences.zh: 東海王越等執乂，送于金墉城。

translations.literal: Prince of Donghai Yue and others seized Yi and sent him to the Golden Moat bastion.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue and the eastern lords seized Yi and locked him in Jinyong fortress.

sentences.zh: 方使郅輔取乂還營，炙殺之。

translations.literal: Fang sent Zhi Fu to fetch Yi back to camp and roasted him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Fang sent Zhi Fu to drag Yi back and burned him alive.

sentences.zh: 於是大掠洛中官私奴婢萬餘人，而西還長安。

translations.literal: Thereupon he greatly plundered more than ten thousand government and private slave-girls in Luoyang and returned west to Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: He then looted Luoyang of over ten thousand men and women and marched west to Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 顒加方右將軍、馮翊太守。

translations.literal: Yong added Fang general of the right and prefect of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yong promoted him to general of the right and governor of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 蕩陰之役，顒又遣方鎮洛陽，上官已、苗願等距之，大敗而退。

translations.literal: In the Tangyin campaign Yong again dispatched Fang to hold Luoyang; Shangguan Yi, Miao Yuan and others resisted him; he was greatly defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At Tangyin Yong sent Fang back to Luoyang; Shangguan Yi and Miao Yuan shattered his line.

sentences.zh: 清河王覃夜襲已、願，已、願出奔，方乃入洛陽。

translations.literal: Prince of Qinghe Sima Tan by night attacked Yi and Yuan; Yi and Yuan fled out; Fang then entered Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qinghe Sima Tan raided the defenders at night; when they fled, Fang walked into an empty capital.

sentences.zh: 覃于廣陽門迎方而拜，方馳下車扶止之。

translations.literal: Tan at Guangyang Gate welcomed Fang and bowed; Fang galloped down from the carriage to support and stop him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Tan kowtowed at Guangyang Gate; Fang leapt down to raise him.

sentences.zh: 於是復廢皇后羊氏。

translations.literal: Thereupon he again deposed Empress Yang of the Yang clan.
translations.idiomatic: He then deposed Empress Yang again.

sentences.zh: 及帝自鄴還洛，方遣息羆以三千騎奉迎。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned from Ye to Luoyang, Fang dispatched his son Pi with three thousand horse to escort the welcome.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled from Ye to Luoyang, Fang sent his son Pi with three thousand riders to escort him.

sentences.zh: 將渡河橋，方又以所乘陽燧車、青蓋素升三百人為小鹵簿，迎帝至芒山下。

translations.literal: About to cross the river bridge, Fang again with the yang-sui carriage he rode, green canopy and plain palanquin three hundred men as minor escort, welcomed the emperor to below Mang Hill.
translations.idiomatic: At the crossing he supplied the imperial sun-mirror carriage, green canopy, and three hundred attendants in miniature escort as far as Mang Hill.

sentences.zh: 方自帥萬餘騎奉雲母輿及旌旗之飾，衛帝而進。

translations.literal: Fang himself commanded more than ten thousand horse bearing mica palanquin and banner ornaments, guarding the emperor and advancing.
translations.idiomatic: He personally led ten thousand cavalry with mica palanquins and silken banners to screen the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 初，方見帝將拜，帝下車自止之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Fang saw the emperor was about to bow, the emperor descended the carriage himself and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Fang tried to kowtow, the emperor stepped from his carriage to forbid it.

sentences.zh: 方在洛既久，兵士暴掠，發哀獻皇女墓。

translations.literal: Fang having been long in Luoyang, soldiers violently plundered, digging open Princess Aixian’s tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Fang’s troops had occupied Luoyang so long they grew bored with mere looting and opened Princess Aixian’s tomb.

sentences.zh: 軍人喧喧，無復留意，議欲西遷，尚匿其跡，欲須天子出，因劫移都。

translations.literal: The soldiers clamored without further intent to stay; they deliberated wishing to move west, still hiding their tracks, wishing to wait until the Son of Heaven came out, then by kidnapping shift the capital.
translations.idiomatic: They clamored to move the court west but hid the plan until they could march the emperor out and hijack him.

sentences.zh: 乃請帝謁廟，帝不許。

translations.literal: Thereupon they requested the emperor to visit the ancestral temple; the emperor did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Fang asked leave to escort the emperor to the imperial shrines; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 方遂悉引兵入殿迎帝，帝見兵至，避之于竹林中，軍人引帝出，方於馬上稽首曰：「胡賊縱逸，宿衛單少，陛下今日幸臣壘，臣當捍禦寇難，致死無二。

translations.literal: Fang then led all troops into the hall to welcome the emperor; the emperor seeing troops arrive hid in a bamboo grove; the soldiers pulled the emperor out; Fang on horseback kowtowed, saying, “Hu bandits run wild; the night guard is thin; Your Majesty today favors my camp; your servant will defend against raider hardship, to death without two minds.
translations.idiomatic: Fang then marched into the palace, flushed the emperor from a bamboo grove, and said from horseback, “Barbarians press the frontiers and the palace guard is thin; come to my camp and I will die shielding you.”

sentences.zh: 」於是軍人便亂入宮閣，爭割流蘇武帳而為馬帴。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon the soldiers then disorderly entered palace chambers, competing to cut tasseled martial curtains to make horse cloths.
translations.idiomatic: His men poured into the harem, hacking silk curtains into saddlecloths.

sentences.zh: 方奉帝至弘農，顒遣司馬周弼報方，欲廢太弟，方以為不可。

translations.literal: Fang escorted the emperor to Hongnong; Yong dispatched marshal Zhou Bi to report to Fang, wishing to depose the senior heir; Fang held it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: At Hongnong Yong’s courier Zhou Bi urged deposing the crown prince; Fang refused.

sentences.zh: 帝至長安，以方為中領軍、錄尚書事，領京兆太守。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached Chang’an, he appointed Fang central commandant of the guards, concurrent recorder of the ministry of appointments, concurrent prefect of the capital district.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang’an the emperor named Fang chief of the central guard, recorder of appointments, and governor of the capital district.

sentences.zh: 時豫州刺史劉喬檄稱潁川太守劉輿迫脅范陽王虓距逆詔命，及東海王越等起兵于山東，乃遣方率步騎十萬往討之。

translations.literal: At that time Inspector of Yu Liu Qiao’s call claimed Yingchuan Prefect Liu Yu had coerced Prince of Fanyang Sima Xiao to resist edict commands, and Prince of Donghai Yue and others raised troops in Shandong; [Yong] thereupon dispatched Fang leading infantry and cavalry one hundred thousand to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Qiao’s manifesto accused Liu Yu of forcing Prince Fanyang Sima Xiao to defy the edict and Sima Yue mobilized Shandong, Yong hurled a hundred thousand men under Fang eastward.

sentences.zh: 方屯兵霸上，而劉喬為虓等所破。

translations.literal: Fang encamped troops at Bashang, but Liu Qiao was broken by Xiao and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Fang camped at Bashang while Liu Qiao collapsed before Sima Xiao.

sentences.zh: 顒聞喬敗，大懼，將罷兵，恐方不從，遲疑未決。

translations.literal: Yong hearing Qiao was defeated was greatly afraid, wished to dismiss troops, feared Fang would not obey, hesitated undecided.
translations.idiomatic: Yong panicked at the news yet dared not recall Fang for fear he would mutiny.

sentences.zh: 初，方從山東來，甚微賤，長安富人郅輔厚相供給。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Fang came from Shandong he was very mean and lowly; a Chang’an rich man Zhi Fu supplied him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Years earlier, when Fang was a penniless adventurer from the east, magnate Zhi Fu had bankrolled him.

sentences.zh: 及貴，以輔為帳下督，甚昵之。

translations.literal: When he became noble, he made Fu chief of tent staff and was very intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Fang repaid the debt by making Zhi Fu his household captain and confidant.

sentences.zh: 顒參軍畢垣，河間冠族，為方所侮，忿而說顒曰：「張方久屯霸上，聞山東賊盛，盤桓不進，宜防其未萌。

translations.literal: Yong’s adjutant Bi Yuan, a leading clan of Hejian, was humiliated by Fang; angrily he said to Yong, “Zhang Fang has long encamped at Bashang; hearing Shandong bandits are strong, he loiters without advancing—you should guard before it sprouts.
translations.idiomatic: Adjutant Bi Yuan, a proud noble Yong had assigned to Fang’s staff, seethed at Fang’s insults and whispered to Yong: “Fang idles at Bashang while Shandong swells—cut him before he turns on you.”

sentences.zh: 其親信郅輔具知其謀矣。

translations.literal: His intimate Zhi Fu fully knows his plot.
translations.idiomatic: His favorite Zhi Fu knows every detail of his schemes.”

sentences.zh: 」而繆播等先亦構之，顒因使召輔，垣迎說輔曰：「張方欲反，人謂卿知之。

translations.literal: ” Moreover Miao Bo and others earlier had also framed him; Yong therefore sent to summon Fu; Yuan intercepted and persuaded Fu, saying, “Zhang Fang wishes to rebel; people say you know it.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Bo’s faction had said the same; Yong summoned Zhi Fu, but Bi Yuan waylaid him: “They say you helped Fang plot treason.”

sentences.zh: 王若問卿，何辭以對？

translations.literal: If the prince asks you, with what words will you answer?
translations.idiomatic: When Yong questions you, what will you say?”

sentences.zh: 」輔驚曰：「實不聞方反，為之若何？

translations.literal: ” Fu startled said, “Truly I have not heard Fang rebels; what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Fu stammered, “Rebellion? I never heard—what should I say?”

sentences.zh: 」垣曰：「王若問卿，但言爾爾。

translations.literal: ” Yuan said, “If the prince asks you, only say yes-yes.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan murmured, “Just nod and agree.”

sentences.zh: 不然，必不免禍。

translations.literal: ” Otherwise you will surely not avoid calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise you will not escape the axe.”

sentences.zh: 」輔既入，顒問之曰：「張方反，卿知之乎？

translations.literal: ” Fu having entered, Yong asked him, saying, “Zhang Fang rebels—do you know it?
translations.idiomatic: At the interview Yong demanded, “Is Fang plotting treason?”

sentences.zh: 」輔曰：「爾。

translations.literal: ” Fu said, “Yes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Fu whispered, “Yes.”

sentences.zh: 」顒曰：「遣卿取之可乎？

translations.literal: ” Yong said, “If I send you to take him—can it work?
translations.idiomatic: Yong pressed, “Would you fetch his head for me?”

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「爾。

translations.literal: ” He also said, “Yes.”
translations.idiomatic: Yong added another flat “yes”—the signal Zhi Fu was waiting for.

sentences.zh: 」顒於是使輔送書于方，因令殺之。

translations.literal: ” Yong thereupon ordered Fu to deliver a letter to Fang, and on that pretext ordered him to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Yong told Zhi Fu to hand Zhang Fang a letter, then use the meeting as cover for murder.

sentences.zh: 輔既昵于方，持刀而入，守閣者不疑，因火下發函，便斬方頭。

translations.literal: Fu, being intimate with Fang, entered holding a knife; the gate guards did not suspect; therefore by lamplight he opened the dispatch and immediately cut off Fang’s head.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Fu, still Zhang Fang’s confidant, walked past the guards with a blade, opened the “letter” by candlelight, and struck off Fang’s head.

sentences.zh: 顒以輔為安定太守。

translations.literal: Yong appointed Fu prefect of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Yong rewarded him with the Anding prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初繆播等議斬方，送首與越，冀東軍可罷。

translations.literal: Earlier Miao Bo and others had deliberated executing Fang, sending the head to Yue, hoping the eastern army could cease.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Miao Bo’s faction had urged beheading Fang and shipping his head east to satisfy Sima Yue.

sentences.zh: 及聞方死，更爭入關，顒頗恨之，又使人殺輔。

translations.literal: When they heard Fang had died, they instead competed to enter the pass; Yong resented it somewhat and again sent persons to kill Fu.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Fang was dead, those same easterners rushed the passes anyway; Yong cursed their greed and had Zhi Fu killed too.

sentences.zh: :　　史臣曰：晉氏之禍難薦臻，實始籓翰。

translations.literal: The court historians state: The calamities of the House of Jin piled up without end; they truly began with the bulwark princes.
translations.idiomatic: The compilers write: Jin’s ruin came in waves, and every wave began with the armed princes who were meant to shield the throne.

sentences.zh: 解系等以幹時之用，處危亂之辰，並托跡府朝，參謀王室。

translations.literal: Xie Xi and the others, by timely utility, dwelt in perilous and chaotic times, all entrusting footprints to princely courts and counseling the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: Men like Xie Xi had talent the age demanded, yet they tethered their fortunes to one prince after another while the dynasty collapsed around them.

sentences.zh: 或抗忠盡節，或飾詐懷奸。

translations.literal: Some resisted with loyalty exhausting integrity; others adorned deceit and harbored treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Some died for honest loyalty; others thrived on double-dealing.

sentences.zh: 雖邪正殊途，而咸至誅戮，豈非時艱政紊，利深禍速者乎！

translations.literal: Although wicked and upright were different roads, yet all alike reached execution and slaughter—is it not that the times were hard and government tangled, profit deep and calamity swift!
translations.idiomatic: Wicked or worthy, nearly every man in this roll met a violent end—such is politics when profit outruns principle.

sentences.zh: 古人所以危邦不入，亂邦不居，戒懼於此也。

translations.literal: This is why the ancients feared entering a state in peril and dwelling in a state in chaos, taking warning here.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the sages’ warning: do not enter a tottering state or live in a rebel court.

sentences.zh: 閻鼎

translations.literal: Yan Ding
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ding (western restoration minister).

sentences.zh: 閻鼎，字臺臣，天水人也。

translations.literal: Yan Ding, courtesy name Taichen, was a man of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ding, courtesy Taichen, came from Tianshui commandery.

sentences.zh: 初為太傅東海王越參軍，轉卷令，行豫州刺史事，屯許昌。

translations.literal: First he was adjutant to grand tutor Prince of Donghai Sima Yue, transferred scroll director, acting inspector of Yu province, encamped at Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He began on Sima Yue’s staff, became archives director, and served as acting inspector of Yu with headquarters at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 遭母喪，乃於密縣間鳩聚西州流人數千，欲還鄉里。

translations.literal: Encountering his mother’s mourning, then at Mi county he secretly gathered several thousand western refugees, wishing to return to their home regions.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his mother he mustered thousands of homesick westerners hiding in Mi county.

sentences.zh: 值京師失守，秦王出奔密中，司空荀籓、籓弟司隸校尉組，及中領軍華恆、河南尹華薈，在密縣建立行臺，以密近賊，南趣許潁。

translations.literal: It happened that the capital was lost and the Prince of Qin fled into Mi; minister of works Xun Fan, Fan’s younger brother metropolitan commandant Xun Zu, central commandant of the guards Hua Heng, and Henan prefect Hua Hui were at Mi county establishing a mobile headquarters; because Mi was near bandits, they hastened south toward Xu and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell the Prince of Qin fled to Mi, where Xun Fan, Xun Zu, Hua Heng, and Hua Hui set up a field headquarters; fearing Mi’s exposed position, they pushed south toward the Xu–Ying corridor.

sentences.zh: 司徒左長史劉疇在密為塢主，中書令李暅、太傅參軍騶捷劉蔚、鎮軍長史周顗、司馬李述皆來赴疇。

translations.literal: Steward of the left of the minister of education Liu Chou at Mi was chief of the fort; palace secretariat director Li Xuan, grand tutor’s adjutants Zou Jie and Liu Wei, chief clerk to the army guarding the army Zhou Yi, and marshal Li Shu all came to join Chou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chou of the ministry of education commanded the Mi fortress; Li Xuan, Zou Jie, Liu Wei, Zhou Yi, and Li Shu rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 僉以鼎有才用，且手握強兵，勸籓假鼎冠軍將軍、豫州刺史，蔚等為參佐。

translations.literal: All held that Ding had talent and utility, and moreover grasped strong troops; they urged Fan to grant Ding acting champion general and inspector of Yu, with Wei and others as staff.
translations.idiomatic: They argued that Ding commanded real soldiers and real talent, so Xun Fan should name him champion general and inspector of Yu with the others as aides.

sentences.zh: 鼎少有大志，因西土人思歸，欲立功鄉里，乃與撫軍長史王毗、司馬傳遜懷翼戴秦王之計，謂疇、捷等曰：「山東非霸王處，不如關中。

translations.literal: Ding in youth had great aims; because westerners longed to return west and he wished to merit himself in his home region, then together with chief clerk to the pacification army Wang Pi and marshal Fu Xun he cherished a plan to support the Prince of Qin, saying to Chou, Jie, and others, “Shandong is no place for a hegemon-king; it is not as good as Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Ding nursed large ambitions; playing on westerners’ homesickness he and Wang Pi and Fu Xun urged Liu Chou’s circle: “The central plain cannot sustain a rival king—only Guanzhong can.”

sentences.zh: 」河陽令傅暢遺鼎書，勸奉秦王過洛陽，謁拜山陵，徑據長安，綏合夷晉，興起義眾，克復宗廟，雪社稷之恥。

translations.literal: ” Magistrate of Heyang Fu Chang sent Ding a letter, urging to escort the Prince of Qin past Luoyang, to visit and bow at the mausoleums, go straight to occupy Chang’an, pacify and join barbarian and Jin, raise righteous hosts, restore the ancestral temples, and wipe away the shame on the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chang of Heyang wrote urging him to march the Prince of Qin through Luoyang, pay homage at the tombs, seize Chang’an, rally Di and Chinese alike, and rebuild the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 鼎得書，便欲詣洛，流人謂北道近河，懼有抄截，欲南自武關向長安。

translations.literal: Ding received the letter and wished to go to Luoyang; the refugees said the northern road neared the river and they feared raiding interception; they wished south from Wu Pass toward Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: Ding wanted the northern route through Luoyang; the refugees, fearing river pirates, voted for Wu Pass into Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 疇等皆山東人，咸不願西入，荀籓及疇、捷等並逃散。

translations.literal: Chou and others were all Shandong men and none wished to go west; Xun Fan together with Chou, Jie, and others all fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chou and the easterners refused to march west; Xun Fan and the rest slipped away overnight.

sentences.zh: 鼎追籓不及，暅等見殺，唯顗、述走得免。

translations.literal: Ding pursued Fan but did not overtake him; Xuan and others were killed; only Yi and Shu fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Ding failed to catch Xun Fan; Li Xuan died in the chaos while Zhou Yi and Li Shu escaped.

sentences.zh: 遂奉秦王行，止上洛，為山賊所襲，殺百餘人，率餘眾西至藍田。

translations.literal: Thereupon he escorted the Prince of Qin on the march, halted at Shangluo, was raided by mountain bandits, more than a hundred killed, led the remainder of the host west to Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: He shepherded the Prince of Qin toward Shangluo, lost a hundred men to brigands, and limped on to Lantian.

sentences.zh: 時劉聰向長安，為雍州刺史賈疋所逐，走還平陽。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Cong was heading toward Chang’an, was driven by inspector of Yong Jia Pi, and fled back to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Liu Cong advanced on Chang’an until Jia Pi drove him back to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 疋遣人奉迎秦王，遂至長安，而與大司馬南陽王保、衛將軍梁芬、京兆尹梁綜等並同心推戴，立王為皇太子，登壇告天，立社稷宗廟，以鼎為太子詹事，總攝百揆。

translations.literal: Pi sent men to escort welcome the Prince of Qin; thereupon he reached Chang’an, and together with grand marshal Prince of Nanyang Sima Bao, guard general Liang Fen, Jingzhao prefect Liang Zong, and others with one heart they pushed support, established the king as imperial heir apparent, ascended the altar to announce to Heaven, established altars of soil and grain and ancestral temples, appointed Ding grand mentor to the heir, overall holding the hundred handles.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Pi’s escort brought the prince into Chang’an, where he, Sima Bao, Liang Fen, Liang Zong, and others enthroned him as crown prince, rebuilt the state altars, and named Ding mentor to the heir with sweeping civil powers.

sentences.zh: 梁綜與鼎爭權，鼎殺綜，以王毗為京兆尹。

translations.literal: Liang Zong and Ding quarreled over power; Ding killed Zong and appointed Wang Pi Jingzhao prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Ding murdered Liang Zong in a turf fight and replaced him with Wang Pi as governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 鼎首建大謀，立功天下。

translations.literal: Ding first established the great plan and merited achievement under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ding had masterminded the restoration and deserved the credit.

sentences.zh: 始平太守曲允、撫夷護軍索綝並害其功，且欲專權，馮翊太守梁緯、北地太守梁肅，並綜母弟，綝之姻也，謀欲除鼎，乃證其有無君之心，專戮大臣，請討之，遂攻鼎。

translations.literal: Shiping prefect Qu Yun and colonel who pacifies the barbarians Suo Chen both envied his achievement, and moreover wished to monopolize power; Fengyi prefect Liang Wei and Beidi prefect Liang Su, both Zong’s younger brothers by the same mother and Chen’s marriage kin, plotted wishing to remove Ding; they therefore bore false witness that he harbored a heart without regard for the lord, specialized in killing great ministers, requested to punish him, thereupon attacked Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yun and Suo Chen, jealous of his clout, incited Liang Wei and Liang Su—brothers of the slain Liang Zong and Suo Chen’s in-laws—to accuse Ding of disloyalty and lese-majesty, then struck his camp.

sentences.zh: 鼎出奔雍，為氐竇首所殺，傳首長安。

translations.literal: Ding fled out to Yong and was killed by Di chief Dou Shou; his head was sent to Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: Ding fled toward Yong and died at the hands of the Di chieftain Dou Shou; his head went to Chang’an on a pike.

sentences.zh: 索靖

translations.literal: Suo Jing
translations.idiomatic: Suo Jing (calligrapher and general).

sentences.zh: 索靖，字幼安，敦煌人也。

translations.literal: Suo Jing, courtesy name You’an, was a man of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Jing, courtesy You’an, hailed from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 累世官族，父湛，北地太守。

translations.literal: For generations an official clan; his father Zhan was prefect of Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had served for generations; his father Suo Zhan governed Beidi.

sentences.zh: 靖少有逸群之量，與鄉人泛衷、張甝、索紾、索永俱詣太學，馳名海內，號稱「敦煌五龍」。

translations.literal: Jing in youth had capacity surpassing the herd; together with fellow townsman Fan Zhong, Zhang Dan, Suo Zhen, and Suo Yong he all went to the Imperial Academy, his fame galloping within the seas, styled the “Five Dragons of Dunhuang.”
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he towered over peers; with Fan Zhong, Zhang Dan, and the Suo cousins he studied at the academy and became famed as Dunhuang’s “Five Dragons.”

sentences.zh: 四人並早亡，唯靖該博經史，兼通內緯。

translations.literal: The four together died early; only Jing was comprehensive in the classics and histories, and also penetrated inner weft-text apocrypha.
translations.idiomatic: The other four died young; Jing alone mastered the canon, histories, and apocryphal weft books.

sentences.zh: 州辟別駕，郡舉賢良方正，對策高第。

translations.literal: The province summoned him aide-de-camp; the commandery raised him worthy and upright; in the policy examination he ranked high.
translations.idiomatic: The province took him as chief clerk; the commandery nominated him worthy-and-upright; he topped the policy exam.

sentences.zh: 傅玄、張華與靖一面，皆厚與之相結。

translations.literal: Fu Xuan and Zhang Hua, on one meeting with Jing, all treated him thickly and knotted friendship.
translations.idiomatic: A single audience with Fu Xuan and Zhang Hua won him their lasting patronage.

sentences.zh: 拜駙馬都尉，出為西域戊己校尉長史。

translations.literal: He was appointed commandant of the carriage horses, went out as chief clerk to the Wu–ji colonel of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: He became commandant of the consort’s carriage horses, then chief clerk on the western frontier staff.

sentences.zh: 太子僕同郡張勃特表，以靖才藝絕人，宜在臺閣，不宜遠出邊塞。

translations.literal: Crown prince’s steward from the same commandery Zhang Bo specially memorialized, because Jing’s talent and arts surpassed others, he ought to be at the terrace and pavilion, not be sent out far to the border passes.
translations.idiomatic: His townsman Zhang Bo, steward to the heir, begged the throne to keep such a genius in the capital rather than waste him beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 武帝納之，擢為尚書郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu accepted it and promoted him gentleman of the ministries.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu agreed and pulled him into the ministry as a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 與襄陽羅尚、河南潘岳、吳郡顧榮同官，咸器服焉。

translations.literal: Together with Xiangyang Luo Shang, Henan Pan Yue, and Wu commandery Gu Rong he held the same office; all esteemed and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He served alongside Luo Shang, Pan Yue, and Gu Rong, each of whom deferred to him.

sentences.zh: 靖與尚書令衛瓘俱以善草書知名，帝愛之。

translations.literal: Jing together with minister of the palace Wei Guan both were famed for skilled cursive script; the emperor loved them.
translations.idiomatic: He and palace minister Wei Guan were celebrated cursive calligraphers; the emperor prized them both.

sentences.zh: 瓘筆勝靖，然有楷法，遠不能及靖。

translations.literal: Guan’s brush surpassed Jing’s, yet having regular-script method, he was far unable to match Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guan’s brush was stronger overall, but in the disciplined elegance of draft script he could not touch Suo Jing.

sentences.zh: 靖在臺積年，除雁門太守，遷魯相，又拜酒泉太守。

translations.literal: Jing at the terrace many years, removed as prefect of Wild Goose Gate, promoted minister tutor of Lu, again appointed prefect of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: After long service at court he became prefect of Yanmen, then tutor to the Lu kingdom, then governor of Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 惠帝即位，賜爵關內侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui ascended, he was granted noble rank within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui ennobled him as a secondary marquis within the passes.

sentences.zh: 靖有先識遠量，知天下將亂，指洛陽宮門銅駝，歎曰：「會見汝在荊棘中耳！」

translations.literal: Jing had foreknowledge and far-reaching measure, knew the realm would soon be in chaos, pointed at the bronze camels at Luoyang’s palace gate, sighed, saying, “I shall see you amid brambles!”
translations.idiomatic: He foresaw chaos, pointed at the palace bronze camels, and muttered, “One day I will find you buried in thorns.”

sentences.zh: 元康中，西戎反叛，拜靖大將軍梁王肜左司馬，加蕩寇將軍，屯兵粟邑，擊賊，敗之。

translations.literal: In the Yuankang era the western tribes rebelled; he was appointed left marshal to grand general Prince of Liang Sima Yong, added general who smashes bandits, encamped troops at Suiyi, struck the bandits, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuankang’s western rising he joined Sima Yong’s staff as left marshal and general who smashes bandits, camped at Suiyi, and broke the raiders.

sentences.zh: 遷始平內史。

translations.literal: He was promoted interior minister of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: His next post was interior minister of Shiping commandery.

sentences.zh: 及趙王倫篡位，靖應三王義舉，以左衛將軍討孫秀有功，加散騎常侍，遷後將軍。

translations.literal: When King of Zhao Lun usurped, Jing answered the righteous rising of the three kings; as general of the left guard he punished Sun Xiu with merit, added cavalier attendant in regular attendance, promoted rear general.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Lun seized the throne, Suo Jing fought for the three princes as general of the left guard, crushed Sun Xiu, earned the right to attend the emperor, and rose to rear general.

sentences.zh: 太安末，河間王顒舉兵向洛陽，拜靖使持節、監洛城諸軍事、遊擊將軍，領雍、秦、涼義兵，與賊戰，大破之，靖亦被傷而卒，追贈太常，時年六十五。

translations.literal: At the end of Tai’an, Prince of Hejian Yong raised troops toward Luoyang; Jing was appointed bearer of the staff of authority, overseer of Luoyang city military affairs, raiding general, commanding Yong–Qin–Liang righteous troops; fighting with bandits he greatly broke them; Jing also was wounded and died; posthumously awarded minister of cults; at that time sixty-five sui.
translations.idiomatic: In Tai’an’s closing months Yong marched east; Suo Jing held Luoyang as raiding general with staff, commanding Di and Qiang auxiliaries, shattered the attackers, and died of wounds at sixty-five; the court enshrined him as minister of cults.

sentences.zh: 後又贈司空，進封安樂亭侯，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: Later again awarded minister of works, advanced enfeoffment village marquis of Anle, posthumous name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posthumously named minister of works, village marquis of Anle, with the posthumous epithet Zhuang (“Stalwart”).

sentences.zh: 靖著《五行三統正驗論》，辯理陰陽氣運。

translations.literal: Jing composed “Discourse on the Five Phases and Three Unities Correct Verification,” disputing principle of yin–yang and qi revolutions.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a treatise on the five phases and the three unities to explain cosmic cycles.

sentences.zh: 又撰《索子》、《晉詩》各二十卷。

translations.literal: He also compiled Suozi and Jin Poems, each twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled twenty scrolls each of Suozi and Jin Poems.

sentences.zh: 又作《草書狀》，其辭曰：

translations.literal: He also composed “Form of Cursive Script,” its wording saying:
translations.idiomatic: He likewise drafted the descriptive rhapsody “Portrait of Cursive Script,” which opens:
The editors mark an omitted passage where the rhapsody’s main text stood.

sentences.zh: 先時，靖行見姑臧城南石地，曰：「此後當起宮殿。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jing was traveling he saw south of Guzang city stone ground, said, “Hereafter here will rise palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: Once, passing the stone plain south of Guzang, he prophesied, “Palaces will rise here.”

sentences.zh: 」至張駿，於其地立南城，起宗廟，建宮殿焉。

translations.literal: ” Down to Zhang Jun, on that ground he established the southern city, raised ancestral temples, and built palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhang Jun’s Later Liang the prophecy came true: he walled the southern quarter, raised temples, and built palaces on that very soil.

sentences.zh: 靖有五子：鯁、綣、璆、聿、綝，皆舉秀才。

translations.literal: Jing had five sons: Geng, Quan, Qiu, Yu, and Chen; all were raised cultivated talent.
translations.idiomatic: His five sons—Geng, Quan, Qiu, Yu, and Chen—all passed the cultivated-talent exam.

sentences.zh: 聿，安昌鄉侯，卒。

translations.literal: Yu was village marquis of Anxiang and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yu held the village marquisate of Anxiang and died young.

sentences.zh: 少子綝最知名。

translations.literal: The youngest son Chen was most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: The youngest, Chen, became the most famous.
The biography continues with his youngest son.

sentences.zh: 少子 綝

translations.literal: Youngest son: Chen
translations.idiomatic: The youngest son was Chen.

sentences.zh: =綝字巨秀，少有逸群之量，靖每曰；

translations.literal: Chen, courtesy name Juxiu, in youth had capacity surpassing the herd; Jing often said:
translations.idiomatic: Suo Chen, courtesy Juxiu, showed the same precocious talent; his father used to say:

sentences.zh: 「綝廊廟之才，非簡劄之用，州郡吏不足汗吾兒也。

translations.literal: “Chen has the talent of the court and temple, not the use of slips and notes; prefectures and commanderies as clerks are not enough to soil my son.”
translations.idiomatic: “This boy belongs in the high councils, not copying documents; a county post would insult him.”

sentences.zh: 」舉秀才，除郎中。

translations.literal: ” He was raised cultivated talent, removed gentleman of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the cultivated-talent exam and entered the palace as a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 嘗報兄仇，手殺三十七人，時人壯之。

translations.literal: Once he avenged his elder brother, personally killing thirty-seven men; people of the time thought him stalwart.
translations.idiomatic: To avenge a brother he slew thirty-seven men single-handed; contemporaries called him fearless.

sentences.zh: 俄轉太宰參軍，除好畤令，人為黃門侍郎，出參征西軍事，轉長安令，在官有稱。

translations.literal: Shortly transferred adjutant to the grand steward, removed magistrate of Haozhi, entered as gentleman of the Yellow Gates, went out as adjutant on western expedition military affairs, transferred magistrate of Chang’an, and at office had praise.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the grand steward’s staff, governed Haozhi, served in the Yellow Gate, joined the western headquarters, and won praise as Chang’an’s magistrate.

sentences.zh: 及成都王穎劫遷惠帝幸鄴，穎為王浚所破，帝遂播越。

translations.literal: When Prince of Chengdu Ying hijacked and moved Emperor Hui to fortunate Ye, Ying was broken by Wang Jun, and the emperor thereupon wandered in exile.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Ying dragged Emperor Hui to Ye and then collapsed before Wang Jun, the sovereign was cast adrift again.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒使張方及綝東迎乘輿，以功拜鷹楊將軍，轉南陽王模從事中郎。

translations.literal: Prince of Hejian Yong ordered Zhang Fang and Chen east to welcome the imperial carriage; by merit he was appointed general who raises hawks, transferred aide in Prince of Nanyang Sima Mo’s bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yong sent Zhang Fang and Suo Chen east to recover the emperor; Chen earned the generalship of the hawk standard and a post on Sima Mo’s staff.

sentences.zh: 劉聰侵掠關東，以綝為奮威將軍以禦之，斬聰將呂逸，又破聰党劉豐，遷新平太守。

translations.literal: Liu Cong raided east of the pass; [the court] appointed Chen general who rouses might to resist him; he beheaded Cong’s general Lü Yi, again broke Cong’s faction Liu Feng, promoted prefect of Xinping.
translations.idiomatic: Against Liu Cong’s raids he was named general who rouses might, cut down Lü Yi, shattered Liu Feng, and became prefect of Xinping.

sentences.zh: 聰將蘇鐵、劉五斗等劫掠三輔，除綝安西將軍、馮翊太守。

translations.literal: Cong’s generals Su Tie, Liu Wudou, and others plundered the three approaches; Chen was appointed general who pacifies the west and prefect of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Tie and Liu Wudou ravaged the capital approaches, Chen took the banners of general who pacifies the west and governor of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 綝有威恩，華夷向服，賊不敢犯。

translations.literal: Chen had awe and kindness; Chinese and barbarians turned and submitted; bandits did not dare offend.
translations.idiomatic: His blend of terror and mercy made Chinese and tribesmen alike obey; raiders avoided his borders.

sentences.zh: 及懷帝蒙塵，長安又陷，模被害，綝泣曰：「與其俱死，寧為伍子胥。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai suffered dust and Chang’an again fell, Mo was killed; Chen wept, saying, “Rather than die with him, I would be Wu Zixu.”
translations.idiomatic: After Huai’s capture and Mo’s murder he swore, “I will not die quietly—I will be another Wu Zixu.”

sentences.zh: 」乃赴安定，與雍州刺史賈疋、扶風太守梁綜、安夷護軍麹允等糾合義眾，頻破賊黨，修復舊館，遷定宗廟。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he rushed to Anding, together with inspector of Yong Jia Pi, Fengyi prefect Liang Zong, colonel who pacifies the barbarians Qu Yun, and others gathered righteous hosts, repeatedly broke bandit factions, repaired the old lodges, advanced and settled the ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: He rode to Anding, joined Jia Pi, Liang Zong, and Qu Yun, rallied loyalists, cleared the approaches, and rebuilt the imperial shrines.

sentences.zh: 進救新平，小大百戰，綝手擒賊帥李羌，與閻鼎立秦王為皇太子，及即尊位，是為湣帝。

translations.literal: Advancing to relieve Xinping, in battles large and small a hundred times, Chen personally captured bandit chief Li Qiang, together with Yan Ding established the Prince of Qin as imperial heir apparent, and when he ascended the honored position, this is Emperor Min.
translations.idiomatic: He fought a hundred actions to relieve Xinping, seized the rebel Li Qiang, and with Yan Ding enthroned the Prince of Qin—later Emperor Min.

sentences.zh: 綝遷侍中、太僕，以首迎大駕、升壇授璽之功，封弋居伯。

translations.literal: Chen was promoted palace attendant, minister coachman, by merit of first welcoming the great chariot and ascending the altar to hand the seal, enfeoffed marquis of Yiju.
translations.idiomatic: For escorting the throne and presenting the seal he became palace attendant, minister coachman, and marquis of Yiju.

sentences.zh: 又遷前將軍、尚書右僕射、領吏部、京兆尹，加平東將軍，進號征東。

translations.literal: Again promoted forward general, right vice-director of the ministry of appointments, concurrent personnel selection, Jingzhao prefect, added general who pacifies the east, advanced title general of the east.
translations.idiomatic: He added forward general, right vice-director of personnel, concurrent Jingzhao governor, and general who pacifies the east, then general of the east.

sentences.zh: 尋又詔曰：「朕昔遇厄運，遭家不造，播越宛楚，爰失舊京。

translations.literal: Shortly again an edict said, “We formerly encountered ill fortune, suffered the house not made, wandered lost in Wan and Chu, thereby losing the old capital.
translations.idiomatic: An edict soon read: “I once fled disaster, wandered through Wan and Chu, and lost the old capital.

sentences.zh: 幸宗廟寵靈，百辟宣力，得從籓衛，托乎群公之上。

translations.literal: Fortunately the ancestral temples’ numinous favor, the hundred officers exerted strength, enabled us to follow the screen guard and be placed above the host of dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Only because the spirits and ministers fought did I return atop the feudatory host.

sentences.zh: 社稷之不隕，實公是賴，宜贊百揆，傅弼朕躬。

translations.literal: That the altars of soil and grain did not fall was truly relying on the duke; you ought to assist the hundred handles and tutor and aid our person.
translations.idiomatic: The realm survives thanks to you; take charge of all offices and steady the throne.

sentences.zh: 其授衛將軍，領太尉，位特進，軍國之事悉以委之。」

translations.literal: We appoint you guard general, concurrent grand commandant, rank specially advanced; military and state affairs are entirely entrusted to you.”
translations.idiomatic: We name you guard general, grand commandant, specially advanced in rank, with every civil and military file on your desk.”

sentences.zh: 及劉曜侵逼王城，以綝為都督征東大將軍，持節討之。

translations.literal: When Liu Yao pressed the royal city, Chen was appointed area commander, general of the east expedition, bearer of the staff of authority to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yao besieged Chang’an, Chen took staff as supreme commander against him.

sentences.zh: 破曜呼日逐王呼延莫，以功封上洛郡公，食邑萬戶，拜夫人荀氏為新豐君，子石元為世子，賜子弟二人鄉亭侯。

translations.literal: He broke Yao’s Chanyu-of-the-day title king Huyan Mo; by merit he was enfeoffed duke of Shangluo commandery, food households ten thousand; his lady Xun was invested lady of Xinfeng; his son Shiyuan was heir; two younger sons were granted village marquisates.
translations.idiomatic: He shattered Liu Yao’s vanguard Huyan Mo, earned the duchy of Shangluo with ten thousand households, ennobled Lady Xun, named his heir Shiyuan, and enfeoffed two younger sons.

sentences.zh: 劉曜入關芟麥苗，綝又擊破之。

translations.literal: Liu Yao entered the pass to mow wheat seedlings; Chen again broke him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yao slipped in to burn the winter wheat, Chen routed him again.

sentences.zh: 自長安伐劉聰，聰將趙染杖其累捷，有自矜之色，帥精騎數百與綝戰，大敗之，染單馬而走。

translations.literal: Campaigning from Chang’an against Liu Cong, Cong’s general Zhao Ran relied on his repeated victories, had a self-priding expression, led picked horse several hundred to fight Chen, greatly defeated him; Ran on a single horse fled.
translations.idiomatic: Marching east against Liu Cong, Chen met Zhao Ran, who swaggered on past victories; Chen shattered his elite cavalry and sent Ran fleeing alone.

sentences.zh: 轉驃騎大將軍、尚書左僕射、錄尚書，承制行事。

translations.literal: He was transferred general-in-chief who displays might, left vice-director of the ministry of appointments, recorder of the ministry of appointments, acting by delegated authority.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to general-in-chief who displays might, left vice-director, and recorder of appointments with full delegated powers.

sentences.zh: 劉曜復率眾人馮翊，帝累徵兵于南陽王保，保左右議曰；

translations.literal: Liu Yao again led a host into Fengyi; the emperor repeatedly summoned troops from Prince of Nanyang Bao; Bao’s attendants deliberated, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao struck Fengyi again; Min begged Sima Bao for reinforcements, but Bao’s staff murmured:

sentences.zh: 「蝮蛇在手，壯士解其腕。

translations.literal: “When the pit viper is in the hand, a stalwart man cuts off his wrist.
translations.idiomatic: “Grip a pit viper and a hero severs his own wrist.”

sentences.zh: 且斷隴道，以觀其變。

translations.literal: ” Moreover cut off the Long road and observe the change.
translations.idiomatic: “Sever the Long Road and watch how the crisis plays out.”

sentences.zh: 」從事中郎裴詵曰：「蛇已螫頭，頭可截不？

translations.literal: ” Aide Pei Shen said, “The snake has already stung the head—can the head be cut off?
translations.idiomatic: Adjutant Pei Shen shot back, “The viper has already struck the head—do you cut off the head?”

sentences.zh: 」保以胡崧行前鋒都督，須諸軍集，乃當發。

translations.literal: ” Bao made Hu Song advance vanguard area commander; he waited for the various hosts to gather, only then would set out.
translations.idiomatic: Bao still named Hu Song vanguard and refused to march until every column had massed.

sentences.zh: 麹允欲挾天子趣保，綝以保必逞私欲，乃止。

translations.literal: Qu Yun wished to seize the Son of Heaven and hasten to Bao; Chen because Bao would surely indulge private desire, thereupon stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yun wanted to drag the emperor west to Bao; Chen blocked the scheme, sure Bao would pocket the throne.

sentences.zh: 自長安以西，不復奉朝廷。

translations.literal: West of Chang’an they no longer obeyed the court.
translations.idiomatic: West of the pass no one obeyed Luoyang anymore.

sentences.zh: 百官饑乏，采穭自存。

translations.literal: The hundred officials hungered and lacked, gathered wild grain husks to preserve themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers starved and scraped the hills for wild grain.

sentences.zh: 時三秦人尹桓、解武等數千家，盜發漢霸、杜二陵，多獲珍寶。

translations.literal: At that time several thousand households of three-Qin men Yin Huan, Xie Wu, and others, robbed open Han Emperor Ba’s and Du’s two tombs, obtaining much treasure.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of Qin refugees led by Yin Huan and Xie Wu plundered the tombs of Emperors Ba and Du of Han, hauling out jewels.

sentences.zh: 帝問綝曰：「漢陵中物何乃多邪？

translations.literal: The emperor asked Chen, saying, “Why are things in Han tombs so numerous?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Suo Chen why Han graves held such wealth.

sentences.zh: 」綝對曰：「漢天子即位一年而為陵，天下貢賦三分之，一供宗廟，一供賓客，一充山陵。

translations.literal: ” Chen answered, saying, “Han Son of Heaven at accession one year then made a tomb; the realm’s tribute and tax were divided in three: one supplied the ancestral temples, one supplied guests, one filled the hills and tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Chen explained: “Every Han emperor began his mausoleum in his first year and split tribute three ways—for the temples, for diplomacy, and for the tomb.”

sentences.zh: 漢武帝饗年久長，比崩而茂陵不復容物，其樹皆已可拱。

translations.literal: ” Emperor Wu of Han enjoyed years long; compared to his death Maoling could no longer hold objects; its trees were already such that one could span them with arms.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu lived so long that Maoling overflowed with treasure while its cypresses grew thick as a man’s embrace.

sentences.zh: 赤眉取陵中物不能減半，於今猶有朽帛委積，珠玉未盡。

translations.literal: ” The Red Eyebrows took objects from the tombs and could not reduce them by half; to this day there are still rotten silks piled in heaps, pearls and jade not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Even the Red Eyebrows could not carry half away; rotting brocade and jade still litter those vaults.

sentences.zh: 此二陵是儉者耳，亦百世之誡也。」

translations.literal: ” These two tombs were frugal ones—yet also a warning for a hundred generations.”
translations.idiomatic: “Those were the modest tombs—imagine the rest. Let that be a lesson for every dynasty.”

sentences.zh: 後劉曜又率眾圍京城、綝與麹允固守長安小城。

translations.literal: Later Liu Yao again led a host to besiege the capital city; Chen together with Qu Yun firmly defended the small city of Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yao returned to ring Chang’an, Suo Chen and Qu Yun held the inner citadel.

sentences.zh: 胡崧承檄奔命，破曜於靈臺。

translations.literal: Hu Song answering a call rushed to duty, broke Yao at the Spirit Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Song answered the muster and shattered Liu Yao at the Spirit Terrace.

sentences.zh: 崧慮國家威舉，則麹、索功盛，乃案兵渭北，遂還槐里。

translations.literal: Song feared that if the state’s awe were raised, then Qu’s and Chen’s merit would be great; thereupon he halted troops north of the Wei and returned to Huaili.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Song dreaded seeing Qu and Suo steal the glory, so he froze his army on the north bank of the Wei and withdrew to Huaili.

sentences.zh: 城中饑窘，人相食，死亡逃奔不可制，唯涼州義眾千人守死不移。

translations.literal: Inside the city hunger was desperate; people ate one another; death, flight, and scattering could not be controlled; only a thousand righteous hosts from Liangzhou guarded to death and did not move.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the walls men starved and cannibalized one another; only a thousand Liangzhou loyalists stood their ground to the last breath.

sentences.zh: 帝使侍中宋敞送箋降於曜。

translations.literal: The emperor sent palace attendant Song Chang to deliver a note surrendering to Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min dispatched Song Chang with a letter of capitulation to Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 綝潛留敞，使其子說曜曰：「今城中食猶足支一歲，未易可克也。

translations.literal: Chen secretly detained Chang, sent his son to persuade Yao, saying, “Now food in the city is still enough to support one year; it is not easy to overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Chen held Song Chang hostage and sent his own son to Liu Yao with a lie: “We still have a year’s provisions—

sentences.zh: 若許綝以車騎、儀同、萬戶郡公者，請以城降。

translations.literal: ” If you grant Chen chariot-and-cavalry commander, ceremonial parity with the Three Excellencies, and duke of a ten-thousand-household commandery, then I request to surrender the city.
translations.idiomatic: make Suo Chen chariot general with Three Excellencies honors and a ten-thousand-household duchy, and we will open the gates.”

sentences.zh: 」曜斬而送之曰：「帝王之師，以義行也。

translations.literal: ” Yao executed him and sent him back, saying, “An army of a Son of Heaven acts by righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Yao executed the envoy and returned his head with a message: “Kings wage righteous war—

sentences.zh: 孤將軍十五年，未嘗以譎詭敗人，必窮兵極勢，然後取之。

translations.literal: ” I, lone general, fifteen years, have never used deceit and guile to defeat people; I must exhaust arms and utmost force, then take them.
translations.idiomatic: I have campaigned fifteen years without buying victory by treachery; I break cities by force alone.”

sentences.zh: 今索綝所說如是，天下之惡一也，輒相為戮之。

translations.literal: ” Now what Suo Chen says is like this—one with the worst under heaven—let him be killed for one another.
translations.idiomatic: “Suo Chen’s bargain is the vilest treason—execute him as an example.”

sentences.zh: 若審兵食未盡者，便可勉強固守。

translations.literal: ” If indeed arms and food are not yet exhausted, then you may strive to defend firmly.
translations.idiomatic: “If you truly have grain and spears left, defend as long as you can.”

sentences.zh: 如其糧竭兵微，亦宜早悟天命。

translations.literal: ” If like that grain is exhausted and troops slight, you also ought early to apprehend Heaven’s mandate.
translations.idiomatic: “If you are hollow, read Heaven’s will and yield.”

sentences.zh: 孤恐霜威一震，玉石俱摧。

translations.literal: ” I fear once frost-like majesty shakes once, jade and stone together will be crushed.
translations.idiomatic: “Once my host strikes, jade and tile will shatter together.”

sentences.zh: 」及帝出降，綝隨帝至平陽，劉聰以其不忠於本朝，戮之於東市。

translations.literal: ” When the emperor came out to surrender, Chen followed the emperor to Pingyang; Liu Cong because he was not loyal to his original court, executed him in the eastern market.
translations.idiomatic: When Min walked out to yield, Suo Chen followed him to Pingyang; Liu Cong judged him disloyal and had him cut down in the eastern market.

sentences.zh: 賈疋

translations.literal: Jia Pi
translations.idiomatic: Jia Pi (general who restored the western throne).

sentences.zh: 賈疋，字彥度，武威人，魏太尉詡之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Jia Pi, courtesy name Yandu, was a man of Wuwei, great-grandson of Wei grand commandant Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Pi, courtesy Yandu, of Wuwei, was the great-grandson of the Wei strategist Jia Xu.

sentences.zh: 少有志略，器望甚偉，見之者莫不悅附，特為武夫之所瞻仰，願為致命。

translations.literal: In youth he had aims and stratagems; his bearing and reputation were very grand; those who saw him none did not joyfully attach; especially military men looked up to him, willing to give life for him.
translations.idiomatic: He combined ambition with charisma; soldiers idolized him and would die at his word.

sentences.zh: 初辟公府，遂曆顯職，遷安定太守。

translations.literal: First summoned clerk to the excellencies, thereupon passed through eminent posts, promoted prefect of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the central offices, he rose through prominent posts to governor of Anding.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史丁綽，貪橫失百姓心，乃譖疋于南陽王模，模以軍司謝班伐之。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yong Ding Chuo was greedy and overbearing and lost the common people’s hearts; he therefore slandered Pi to Prince of Nanyang Mo; Mo used army director Xie Ban to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Yong inspector Ding Chuo was so corrupt that he lost the region; he slandered Jia Pi to Sima Mo, who sent Xie Ban against him.

sentences.zh: 疋奔瀘水，與胡彭蕩仲及氐竇首結為兄弟，聚眾攻班。

translations.literal: Pi fled to the Lu River, with the Hu Peng Dangzhong and Di chief Dou Shou swore brotherhood, gathered a host and attacked Ban.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Pi fled to the Lu, allied with the chieftain Peng Dangzhong and Dou Shou, and turned on Xie Ban.

sentences.zh: 綽奔武都，疋復入安定，殺班。

translations.literal: Chuo fled to Wudu; Pi again entered Anding and killed Ban.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Chuo bolted to Wudu while Jia Pi reoccupied Anding and killed Xie Ban.

sentences.zh: 湣帝以疋為驃騎將軍、雍州刺史，封酒泉公。

translations.literal: Emperor Min appointed Pi general-in-chief who displays might, inspector of Yong, enfeoffed duke of Jiuquan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min named him general-in-chief who displays might, inspector of Yong, and duke of Jiuquan.

sentences.zh: 時諸郡百姓饑饉，白骨蔽野，百無一存。

translations.literal: At that time the common people of the various commanderies starved; white bones covered the wilds; not one in a hundred survived.
translations.idiomatic: Famine stripped the commanderies until bones whitened the fields—perhaps one soul in a hundred still drew breath.

sentences.zh: 疋帥戎晉二萬餘人，將伐長安，西平太守竺恢亦固守，劉粲聞之，使劉曜、劉雅及趙染距疋，先攻恢，不克，疋邀擊，大敗之，曜中流矢，退走。

translations.literal: Pi commanded more than twenty thousand Rong and Jin, intending to campaign toward Chang’an; Xiping prefect Zhu Hui also firmly defended; Liu Can hearing it sent Liu Yao, Liu Ya, and Zhao Ran to resist Pi, first attacking Hui, not overcoming him; Pi intercepted and struck, greatly defeated them; Yao was hit by a stray arrow and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Pi led twenty thousand Di and Chinese toward Chang’an; Zhu Hui of Xiping held his walls; Liu Can sent Liu Yao, Liu Ya, and Zhao Ran to block Jia Pi, first besieging Zhu Hui without success; Jia Pi counterattacked, broke the siege, and put a shaft in Liu Yao’s flesh.

sentences.zh: 疋追之，至於甘泉。

translations.literal: Pi pursued them as far as Sweet Springs.
translations.idiomatic: He chased them all the way to Sweet Springs.

sentences.zh: 旋自渭橋襲蕩仲，殺之。

translations.literal: Shortly from the Wei Bridge he raided Dangzhong and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Doubling back across the Wei Bridge he ambushed Peng Dangzhong and killed him.

sentences.zh: 遂迎秦王，奉為皇太子。

translations.literal: Thereupon he welcomed the Prince of Qin, upholding him as imperial heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He then escorted the Prince of Qin to Chang’an as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 後蕩仲子夫護帥群胡攻之，疋敗走，夜墮於澗，為夫護所害。

translations.literal: Later Dangzhong’s son Fuhu commanded a host of Hu to attack him; Pi was defeated and fled, at night fell into a gorge, and was harmed by Fuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Later Peng’s son Fuhu led tribal riders against him; Jia Pi fled by night, fell into a ravine, and Fuhu killed him.

sentences.zh: 疋勇略有志節，以匡復晉室為己任，不幸顛墮，時人咸痛惜之。

translations.literal: Pi was brave in stratagem and had integrity of aim, taking restoration of the house of Jin as his own task; unluckily he stumbled and fell; people of the time all grieved and pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: He had meant to restore the Jin house and died before the work was done; contemporaries mourned him.

sentences.zh: :　　史臣曰：自永嘉蕩覆，宇內橫流，億兆靡依，人神乏主。

translations.literal: The court historians state: From Yongjia’s overturn, within the seas flowed crosswise, hundreds of millions had none to rely on, men and gods lacked a lord.
translations.idiomatic: The compilers write: After Yongjia’s catastrophe the realm dissolved and neither people nor gods had a true sovereign.

sentences.zh: 于時武皇之胤，惟有建興，眾望攸歸，曾無與二。

translations.literal: At that time among Martial Emperor’s descendants there was only the Jianxing reign; the multitude’s hope returned to him; there was none to pair with him.
translations.idiomatic: Among Sima Yan’s progeny only the Jianxing court still commanded universal hope.

sentences.zh: 閻鼎等忠存社稷，志在經綸，乃契闊艱難，扶持幼孺，遂得纂堯承緒，祀夏配天，校績論功，有足稱矣。

translations.literal: Yan Ding and the others were loyal in preserving the altars of soil and grain, their aims set on ordering the realm; therefore they braved hardship, supported the young child, and thereby were able to continue Yao’s line, inherit the thread, sacrifice to Xia and match Heaven; comparing deeds and discussing merit, there is enough to praise.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ding and his allies kept faith with the altars, carried the boy emperor through fire, and briefly restored a legitimate line—deeds worth recording.

sentences.zh: 然而抗滔天之巨寇，接凋弊之餘基，威略未申，尋至傾覆。

translations.literal: Yet they resisted a bandit that covered Heaven, took over a remnant base already withered and ruined, prestige and strategy not yet displayed, and soon arrived at overturn.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they faced invaders who blotted out the sky with only a ruined corner of Jin to stand on, and they fell almost as soon as they rose.

sentences.zh: 昔宗周遭犬戎而東徙，有晉違獷狄而西遷，彼既靈慶悠長，此則禍難遄及，豈湣皇地非奧主，將綝允材謝輔臣，何修短之殊途，而成敗之異數者也？

translations.literal: Formerly the Zhou house encountered Dog Rong and moved east; Jin turned away from fierce Di and moved west; that one’s numinous blessing was long; this one’s disasters arrived swiftly—is it that Emperor Min’s ground was not an inner lord, or that Chen and Yun’s talent fell short of assistant ministers—why different paths of long and short, yet different tallies of success and failure?
translations.idiomatic: Zhou fled the Quanrong eastward yet endured; Jin fled west and perished—was the soil wrong, or were Suo Chen and Qu Yun the wrong ministers, that fate treated the two courts so differently?

translations.literal: 【Appreciation】
translations.idiomatic: Subsection title: “Appreciation.”

sentences.zh: 贊曰：懷惠不競，戚籓力爭。

translations.literal: The appreciation states: Kind Huai did not compete; kin princes strove by force.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy reads: Emperor Huai was gentle and lost the contest; kinsmen princes fought like wolves.

sentences.zh: 狙詐參謀，憑凶亂政。

translations.literal: Sly deceit counseled stratagems; relying on violence they disordered government.
translations.idiomatic: Schemers trafficked in treachery and violence until law collapsed.

sentences.zh: 為惡不已，並羅非命。

translations.literal: Doing evil without stop, together they met untimely death.
translations.idiomatic: Evildoers who would not stop fell one after another to the headsman.

sentences.zh: 解繆忠肅，無聞余慶。

translations.literal: Xie and Miao were loyal and solemn; no hearing of surplus blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The loyal Xies and Miaos won no lasting fortune for their houses.

sentences.zh: 湣皇纂戎，實賴群公。

translations.literal: Emperor Min took up arms; he truly relied on the host of dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min’s brief reign rested on those same loyal lords.

sentences.zh: 鼎圖福始，綝遂凶終。

translations.literal: Ding schemed the blessing’s beginning; Chen met the disaster’s end.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ding opened the road to restoration; Suo Chen closed it in ruin.
